elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a survey or tally of members of the class (e.g. what fruits they like/dislike or their birthday month) and then creating a display wall with pictures and captions

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recreating stories, rhymes or songs through mime, dance or drawing using simple captions, for example, changing the ending of a story or characters within it and presenting the updated story in a performance

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing a character, animal or persona and introducing themselves as that character, using modelled language, for example, 저는 인어공주입니다. 바다에 살아요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and displaying their own or group big books, storyboards or digital texts based on familiar contexts, for example, a digital or physical poster that uses simple descriptive sentences such as 엄마 상어 웃겨요. 아빠 상어 커요.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2U02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: identify sound combinations to produce simple words, and then an increasing number of frequently used words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: differentiating Hangeul from other forms of written expression such as the Roman alphabet, and identifying languages that may be spoken by students within the class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the Korean copula alternates between 2 forms, –예요 and –이에요, and using it with their own names, for example, 케이트예요. ; 마이클이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising 요 as the informal polite sentence ending and identifying that it is most commonly used to show mutual respect in Korean-speaking communities, for example, ending sentences with 요 to be respectful and making this a class norm with teachers modelling it (e.g. 따라하세요 and 안녕하세요?)

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different social situations and using the correct reference to themselves, for example, 저 is used to refer to self and 저는 is used when talking to the teacher; 나 is the casual way to refer to self and 나는 is used when talking to friends

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying that a noun or a pronoun followed by a basic case marker such as -은 / 는, -이 / 가 or -을 / 를, is a chunk which has a syntactic function in a sentence, for example, 우리는, 우리가 or 우리를

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to make a simple question using a common question word, for example, 뭐 좋아해요?, and practising changing simple phrases into simple questions using set of rules

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using high-frequency verbs in a variety of contexts

content_descriptions.text: identify that written and spoken Korean has grammatical structures and other language features that may be similar to or different from English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading simple texts in Korean with support, and noticing similarities and differences between Korean and English text structure such as sentence structure and word order, for example, a verb is located at the end of a sentence in Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a Korean folktale presented in a language other than Korean or English, and noticing similarities and differences between the sounds of each of the languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking students who speak or are familiar with a language other than Korean or English to say a word, phrase or sentence (e.g. ‘I am going to school’) and comparing the grammatical structure of those languages to Korean and English, discussing the similarities and differences

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating words or phrases used in everyday situations from Korean into English and vice versa, noticing how some words do not have a direct translation (e.g. 잘 먹겠습니다, 잘 먹었습니다, 어서 오세요) and thinking about the context, not just the words and phrases when translating

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that spoken Korean uses intonation to show the function of the sentence, whereas punctuation is used in written Korean, for example, using a rising intonation at the end of a spoken question as opposed to a question mark in a written format

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: talking about the use of punctuation and intonation in different languages such as Vietnamese and Chinese

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising plurals are shown by adding 들 after a noun (e.g. 친구들, 음식들) and identifying that it is similar to adding the letter ‘s’ to English nouns to make them plural

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying that punctuation rules are the same in written Korean and written English

elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.elaboration_text: using a pocket chart with individual words and accompanying images to scaffold sentence building

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a scaffold to interchange sentence content and using accompanying images to make concrete connections

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple requests with chants or rhymes using … 주세요 and expressing thanks using 감사합니다 or 고맙습니다, with students taking turns answering in a play-based activity such as a role-play of shopping at a market, for example, 호떡 하나 주세요. 여기 있어요. 감사합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared reading, expressing opinions and responding to questions about a text, for example, 그림 보세요, 뭐있어요? 산 있어요. ; 뭐 보여요? 사람 보여요. ; 좋아요? 네. ; 재미있어요? 아니요. ; 어때요? 좋아요, 재미있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing in the retelling of stories, rhymes and songs through mime or dance in a class performance, or creating a class big book, sequencing main events using key words, phrases and pictures

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with traditions and customs from Korean-speaking communities, for example, decorating a classroom to celebrate 어린이날 or making a paper drum and participating in a performance for 사물놀이

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing words and phrases they know in other languages and cultures with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging actively and sharing the enjoyment of language, culture and texts in a range of ways, for example, listening to and responding to stories, cultural displays and experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Korean landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as 부산 (Pusan) which has the Sino-Korean meaning of ‘Cauldron Mountain’

organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to culture, such as eating 떡국 (rice cake soup), playing 연날리기 (kite flying game) or 흔들북 (drum) for New year

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making traditional Korean patchwork (조각보) using different coloured paper while practising naming the shapes and colours used in their artwork

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading Korean folktale picture books written in English and talking about differences and similarities of other famous folktales from around the world

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2U05 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: reflect on how language, culture and identity are interconnected and discuss how Korean-speaking communities are similar to or different from others
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that there are different ways to greet people in Korean, recognising similarities with and differences from greetings in their own language(s) and culture(s)

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the world contains many different languages spoken by many different communities of speakers and that many people in the world speak more than one language, for example, introducing themselves in whichever language(s) they speak; creating a classroom display with a photo or picture of each student in the class and speech bubbles saying ‘I speak …’ in Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing gestures and body language associated with language use in different cultures, for example, bowing and saying 안녕하세요? when greeting in Korean; learning different ways of kissing on the cheek when saying bonjour in French-speaking cultures; understanding hongi, pressing noses, and saying kia-ora in a traditional Māori greeting

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing different cultural and religious holidays students celebrate at home and sharing different Korean holidays and holiday greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing changes in behaviour or body language when speaking Korean, for example, passing an object to the teacher using 2 hands while saying 선생님, 여기 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying symbols and colours used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and by Korean-speaking communities in a range of contexts, for example, identifying the colours on a range of flags from different countries and communities in Korean, and discussing what the colours represent in English

elaborations.elaboration_text: naming languages they have encountered in everyday life, for example, conducting a class survey to create a list of the languages spoken by their neighbours or classmates

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U05-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing examples of how gestures and body language are similar or different in Korean to the language(s) they speak at home

as_extracts.name: LKORF102-E14
as_extracts.description: They recognise that Korean is spoken in communities and regions in Australia and around the world, and relate this to their own language(s) and culture(s).

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching the countries where different languages are spoken and discussing why the world has many different languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: surveying peers about cultural backgrounds or connections, creating a culture representation map for the class and sharing which languages are used at home or with extended families, in television shows students watch, or by extended family members who live in different countries

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying Korean foods they have tried or heard of and viewing Korean food products available in Australian supermarkets

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing where they heard about Korea and where they heard Korean being used outside of Korean classes

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning about the Korean diaspora and mapping where Korean communities are located worldwide

organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.

elaborations.elaboration_text: learning about famous Korean singers, actors or sports people and finding out about where they live(d) or work(ed), for example, 손흥민, 방탄소년단

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning about various language-speaking communities in Australia and talking about different cultural and religious festivals organised and held by these community groups

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to popular Korean songs that are translated into English such as ‘Baby shark’ and sharing any other popular Korean songs or culture they are familiar with

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U06-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that languages and communities have different protocols regarding the use of terms of respect, for example, there are ways of addressing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using familial terms (e.g. Uncle, Aunty) depending on the relationship, and comparing these terms with those in Korean and/or other languages

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have sophisticated political, economic and social organisation systems, which include but are not limited to family and kinship structures, laws, traditions, customs, land tenure systems and protocols for strong governance and authority.

organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs and chants by singing and performing actions, for example, the ‘가나다라’ song and greeting songs

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing colour-matching games to explore how to describe different colours in Korean, for example, the teacher showing 노란색 colour paper and asking students to find objects of the same colour in the room; cutting papers to make the shapes of Hangeul; talking about the shapes of Hangeul then comparing the shapes to the English and/or another language’s alphabet

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the different languages spoken by members of the class, and listening to the different sounds and ways of saying common expressions such as ‘Good morning’ or ‘My name is …’

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to imaginative texts, such as stories, rhymes and songs, through play-acting, illustration or movement

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the numbers 0–10, for example, counting aloud with a teacher; tracing numbers on paper or in the air; making numbers with playdough

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: tracing simple words in both Korean and English, noticing similarities and differences

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making a dance routine to represent Hangeul shapes in the order of ㄱㄴㄷㄹ

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E01-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing what shapes or objects Hangeul letters remind them of (e.g. ㅎ looks like someone wearing a hat; ㅁ looks like a square), and listening to and watching the teacher’s description of shapes and colours to draw the same shapes and colours

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2E02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop oral language skills through exploring and listening to the sounds and patterns of the language
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Korean Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing the sounds of letters or syllable blocks of Hangeul and noticing that the sounds in Korean may be similar to or different from the sounds in English

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: singing popular children’s songs in Korean and understanding the meanings associated with the English translation, for example, the birthday song or the ‘Heads and shoulders, knees and toes’ song

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reproducing the sounds and rhythms of Korean rhymes and songs with a teacher by reciting, singing and imitating, for example, ‘리리리자로 끝나는 말은’ 오리, 소리, 다리, 우리, 보따리

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with new sets of vocabulary by making concrete associations with them, such as touching and identifying colours in the classroom, or touching and identifying soft-toy animals and naming them

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing likes and dislikes such as colours, animals, foods, sports and hobbies, possibly using images, props or digital prompts

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: facilitating turn-taking and sharing by integrating Korean language expressions into aspects of their play with classmates

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: rehearsing familiar onomatopoeia in animal sounds, for example, 멍멍, 야옹, 음매, 짹짹

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2E03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and respond to greetings, instructions and language relating to their personal world using one- or 2-word responses and/or single-idea phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Korean Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in routine exchanges such as responding to the class roll call, expressing thanks, greeting and taking leave, for example, 네, 아니요, 감사합니다, 안녕하세요, 안녕히 계세요, 안녕히 가세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning how to greet others, using appropriate forms of address and body language, for example, 안녕 with handwaving; 안녕하세요 with bowing

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to basic classroom instructions with appropriate actions, for example, 손 드세요 ; 앉으세요 ; 일어 나세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different languages and cultures of class members and identifying different ways of expressing common words or phrases, such as yes/no, hello/goodbye

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching simple clips showing cultural activities and events in Korean-speaking communities and sharing their responses in guided discussions

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in simple dialogues through play-acting, using toys and books, and practising greetings

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and making simple requests, for example, 안녕하세요 ; 오이 주세요 ; 바나나 주세요 ; 여기 있어요 ; 안녕히 가세요

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2E04 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore connections between language and culture through play and/or imagination
substrand_content_descriptions.strand: Engaging with Korean Language and Culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging with traditions and customs from Korean-speaking communities, for example, decorating a classroom to celebrate 어린이날 or making a paper drum and participating in a performance for 사물놀이

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing words and phrases they know in other languages and cultures with the class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging actively and sharing the enjoyment of language, culture and texts in a range of ways, for example, listening to and responding to stories, cultural displays and experiences

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using gestures, facial expressions and body language through games such as charades, or by incorporating them into stories, plays or songs to enhance meaning

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Korean landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as 부산 (Pusan) which has the Sino-Korean meaning of ‘Cauldron Mountain’

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that music, dance, food, celebrations and games are connected to culture, such as eating 떡국 (rice cake soup), playing 연날리기 (kite flying game) or 흔들북 (drum) for New year

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making traditional Korean patchwork (조각보) using different coloured paper while practising naming the shapes and colours used in their artwork

elaborations.name: VC2LK2E04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading Korean folktale picture books written in English and talking about differences and similarities of other famous folktales from around the world

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2C01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: communicate using formulaic and modelled language relating to aspects of their personal world

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple greetings using appropriate expressions and body language, for example, 안녕하세요? (with a bow), 반가워요 ; 안녕? (with handwaving) 반가워 , and using Korean words and phrases as greetings or farewell, for example, 안녕하세요? ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 안녕? ; 안녕 / 잘 가 / 잘 있어

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting simple conversations about familiar objects, for example, bringing their favourite toy and doing a short show-and-tell; answering simple questions such as 뭐예요? -예요 / 이에요

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: talking about themselves and the immediate environment using modelled language, simple sentence structures, familiar vocabulary, resources and supporting gestures, for example, 우리 학교예요. ; 우리 집이에요. ; 여기는 교실이에요. ; 교실에 컴퓨터가 있어요. ; 저는 -예요 / 이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and responding to simple questions using 네 / 아니요 to express agreement or disagreement, for example, 한국어 공부해요? 네. ; 김치를 좋아해요? 아니요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing information about themselves or another person, and belongings such as describing a person, for example, 마이클이에요. ; 선생님이에요. ; 김치 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding with appropriate actions to simple instructions, such as 따라하세요. ; 일어나세요. ; 앉으세요. ; 인사하세요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in routine exchanges using simple sentence structures in a phone conversation role-play (e.g. ... 있어요 / 없어요, and words such as 네 / 아니요), for example, 미나 있어요? 네. ; 철수 있어요? 아니요. ; 연필 있어요? 아니요, 없어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking about, and expressing likes and dislikes about, topics such as animals, for example, 뭐 좋아해요? 고양이를 좋아해요. ; 곰 좋아해요? 곰 안 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple spoken exchanges in Korean, including appropriate gestures, for example, how to bow and make hand gestures when saying 안녕하세요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C01-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising differences in greetings and expressions in different social settings, such as with people of different ages and/or different degrees of familiarity, for example, 네, 맞아요. as opposed to 응, 맞아.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2C02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in a range of guided language activities using formulaic expressions, and visual and spoken cues

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in songs, rhymes or chants by singing and repeating with actions, for example, 가나다 노래 ; 안녕 노래

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising vocabulary, for example, practising high-frequency verbs using flashcards with images and/or written words, and using gestures to accompany the verbs where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a pocket chart with individual words and accompanying images to scaffold sentence building

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a scaffold to interchange sentence content and using accompanying images to make concrete connections

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making simple requests with chants or rhymes using … 주세요 and expressing thanks using 감사합니다 or 고맙습니다, with students taking turns answering in a play-based activity such as a role-play of shopping at a market, for example, 호떡 하나 주세요. 여기 있어요. 감사합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared reading, expressing opinions and responding to questions about a text, for example, 그림 보세요, 뭐있어요? 산 있어요. ; 뭐 보여요? 사람 보여요. ; 좋아요? 네. ; 재미있어요? 아니요. ; 어때요? 좋아요, 재미있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing in the retelling of stories, rhymes and songs through mime or dance in a class performance, or creating a class big book, sequencing main events using key words, phrases and pictures

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2C03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate key information in a variety of texts with support, and respond using gestures, images, words and/or formulaic phrases
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating understanding and early literacy skills by labelling, matching, clicking and dragging, drawing, miming and using gestures to locate and use information, for example, using magnetic pictures with Korean words on a whiteboard to categorise items under different headings

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding, in Korean or English, to questions about a text, using contextual and visual cues (e.g. listening to a story or viewing a text and identifying and using key words), for example, reading a story that includes body parts and then playing Simon says or labelling a body picture with 머리, 손, 발, 머리

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information from others in a class survey on a topic (e.g. favourite foods), and sharing the information with the class, for example, 안나는 피자를 좋아해요 ; 존은 비빔밥을 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing different types of simple texts (e.g. songs, chants, advertisements, stories) in Korean, and identifying the text type, recognising that texts are used for different purposes and identifying key features of texts when used for different purposes, for example, the phrase 좋아해요 is used in advertisements rather than in a news story

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts by sequencing pictures and simple text in the order that events occurred, or by creating a storyboard to retell a story or information

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that gestures and body language are integral to communicating for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and showing examples of how gestures and body language are also integral to communicating in Korean and the language(s) they may speak at home

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to texts such as digital texts, short videos, stories, rhymes and songs, through play-acting, illustrating, facial expressions or movement, using key words or formulaic phrases

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2C04 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: explore and make meaning from sounds, words and phrases for familiar objects or terms in Korean through play, and discover how languages influence each other
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing formalities in the Korean classroom such as greetings and formulaic expressions, for example, using 안녕하세요? ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 안녕? ; 안녕 ; 잘 가 / 잘 있어

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: including some Korean words and expressions in English conversation when it feels appropriate (e.g. 선생님; I don’t understand; 도와 주세요), noticing changes in behaviour or body language when speaking Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making traditional Korean toys such as 딱지 and practising using common game terms, for example, 이겼다, 졌다, 내 차례

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing well-known children’s games such as hide-and-seek with classroom objects, or 4-square, but using only Korean expressions to communicate

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: performing role-plays, such as buying fruits and vegetables, or acting as a character from a story that is familiar to the class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing Korean children’s games and learning to respond to simple instructions, for example, ‘무궁화 꽃이 피었습니다’ and ‘즐겁게 춤을 추다가 그대로 멈춰라’

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: teaching a family member some Korean expressions or songs such as ‘학교 종’ or ‘생일 노래’ and reporting to the class what they were able to teach

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions in language games such as 코코코 놀이 or 빙고 게임, for example, 코코코 눈! ; 코코코 입!

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2C05 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using words, familiar phrases and modelled language

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a practice conversation to introduce themselves or others, for example, 안녕하세요? 저는 미나예요. ; 만나서 반가워요. 이 친구는 -예요 / 이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: copying and tracing Hangeul letters, syllable blocks and some simple sentences to match a picture, for example, ㄱ, 가, 강, 강 있어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating bilingual captions in Korean and English, for example, a photographic display with handwritten Korean and English captions to present to parents or others about a class event or personal experience such as a sports day or birthday

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching bilingual captions/labels to images of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place locations in their local area or elsewhere in Australia

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a bilingual picture dictionary or making flashcards to use in the classroom for objects such as classroom items (e.g. 창문, 책) and classroom instructions (e.g. 들으세요, 읽으세요, 여기 보세요, 조용히 하세요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a survey or tally of members of the class (e.g. what fruits they like/dislike or their birthday month) and then creating a display wall with pictures and captions

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recreating stories, rhymes or songs through mime, dance or drawing using simple captions, for example, changing the ending of a story or characters within it and presenting the updated story in a performance

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing a character, animal or persona and introducing themselves as that character, using modelled language, for example, 저는 인어공주입니다. 바다에 살아요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2C05-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and displaying their own or group big books, storyboards or digital texts based on familiar contexts, for example, a digital or physical poster that uses simple descriptive sentences such as 엄마 상어 웃겨요. 아빠 상어 커요.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2U01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: imitate the pronunciation and intonation of spoken Korean, and understand how Hangeul sounds are produced and represented

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing Korean and English words used in class to recognise that Korean has its own words, sounds and gestures that are used to make meaning, for example, comparing how Korean students greet teachers and other students to Australian students using English

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: deconstructing vowels and consonants in a letter to pronounce a syllable block, for example, deconstructing 감 to ㄱ, ㅏ, ㅁ and sounding ‘g’, ‘a’, ‘m’ to pronounce 감 as ‘g-a-m’

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing pronunciation, phrasing and intonation skills by singing, reciting and repeating words and phrases in context

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising familiar loan words originating from other languages (e.g. 피아노, 코알라, 초콜렛, 아이스크림) and practising appropriate Korean pronunciation and emphasising syllable blocks

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: differentiating between Korean and English sounds such as comparing names in Korean and English (e.g. 소피 compared with Sophie, 샘 compared with Sam) and using Korean pronunciation when referring to peers in class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the letter and sound relationship in Hangeul (e.g. ㅁ is pronounced as ‘m’) by playing a matching game where half of the students in class are given Hangeul letter cards and the other half are given matching English sounds, and the students try to find their matching partner

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2U02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: identify sound combinations to produce simple words, and then an increasing number of frequently used words and phrases

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: differentiating Hangeul from other forms of written expression such as the Roman alphabet, and identifying languages that may be spoken by students within the class

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing that the Korean copula alternates between 2 forms, –예요 and –이에요, and using it with their own names, for example, 케이트예요. ; 마이클이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising 요 as the informal polite sentence ending and identifying that it is most commonly used to show mutual respect in Korean-speaking communities, for example, ending sentences with 요 to be respectful and making this a class norm with teachers modelling it (e.g. 따라하세요 and 안녕하세요?)

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing different social situations and using the correct reference to themselves, for example, 저 is used to refer to self and 저는 is used when talking to the teacher; 나 is the casual way to refer to self and 나는 is used when talking to friends

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying that a noun or a pronoun followed by a basic case marker such as -은 / 는, -이 / 가 or -을 / 를, is a chunk which has a syntactic function in a sentence, for example, 우리는, 우리가 or 우리를

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how to make a simple question using a common question word, for example, 뭐 좋아해요?, and practising changing simple phrases into simple questions using set of rules

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using high-frequency verbs in a variety of contexts

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK2U03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explore how Hangeul and features of language are used to construct meaning in Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that Hangeul order is different from Roman alphabetical order, for example, 가, 나, 다, 라, ... as opposed to a, b, c ...

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising Hangeul stroke order in writing syllable blocks

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching Korean and English texts, for example, having name tags of students in both Korean and English

elaborations.name: VC2LK2U03-E04 - Korean

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 3 and 4, Korean language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers through purposeful and creative play in structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They use Korean to interact with their peers and teachers and to participate in activities in familiar settings that reflect their interests and capabilities. They use local and digital resources to explore Korean-speaking communities. They continue to receive extensive support through modelling, scaffolding and repetition, as well as the use of targeted resources. 

Students develop active listening skills and use gestures, words and modelled expressions, imitating the sounds, pronunciation and intonation of Korean. Students read and write Hangeul with support; they locate information, respond to and create texts using written and spoken Korean. They access authentic and purpose-developed Korean-language texts such as picture books, stories, songs, digital and animated games, timetables, recipes and advertisements. They recognise the interconnected nature of language, culture and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 4, students use Korean to initiate structured interactions and share information related to the classroom and their personal worlds. They use modelled language to participate in spoken and written activities. They locate and respond to key items of information in texts, using strategies to help interpret and convey meaning in familiar contexts. They use modelled language and basic grammatical structures to create texts in Hangeul, with support.

Students imitate Hangeul sounds, pronunciation and intonation patterns of spoken Korean. They demonstrate their understanding that Korean has non-verbal, spoken and written language conventions and rules to convey meaning. They recognise that some terms have cultural meanings. They identify patterns in Korean and make comparisons between Korean and English, using simple metalanguage. They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E02 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E04 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E02 - Korean

elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising there are different counters used to express numbers in Korean and practising using number expressions with appropriate counters, for example, 한 개, 두 마리, 세 명, 아홉 살, 삼 학년

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using common action and descriptive verbs to describe activities and experiences in daily life, for example, 가요, 일어나요, 들어요, 해요, 좋아요, 나빠요, 착해요

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising using the correct tense when using action and descriptive verbs, for example, 갔어요 / 갈 거예요, 먹었어요 / 먹을 거예요

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E06 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E07 - Korean

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4U03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar Korean language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing language features typically associated with particular texts, for example, the use of imperatives in games such as 주사위를 던져요 and 말을 움직여요

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising Korean in texts such as signage and product labels, and producing their equivalents in English and/or other languages, for example, making an English version of a Korean food product label and emphasising important information such as spice level

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the importance of politeness being explicitly expressed in Korean and comparing this with English and/or other languages, for example, 만나서 반가워요 as opposed to ‘Nice to meet you’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing to practise answering negative questions by agreeing or disagreeing, for example, 안 했어요? 네, 안 했어요. / 아니요, 했어요. ; 밥 안 먹었어요? 네, 안 먹었어요. / 아니요, 먹었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding different aspects of Korean, English and/or other languages and culture such as naming conventions, and explaining differences in word order and spacing, for example, 박준호 as opposed to ‘John Smith’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a short video clip and identifying non-verbal expressions that are typical or expected in communication in different cultures, for example, making or avoiding eye contact, bowing, nodding, pointing

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing parts of a sentence using metalanguage (e.g. noun, verb, adverb, adjective) to describe words, and noticing the word order and patterns

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the influence of Korean on other languages, and the influence of other languages such as Chinese, Japanese, English, French and Italian on Korean over time, for example, sharing examples of words of Korean origin that have been added to the English dictionary (e.g. hallyu, kimchi, mukbang)

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the different ways of naming, greeting and addressing someone (e.g. by given name or title), including the selective use of honorifics and aspects of body language such as making or avoiding eye contact

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place on which they live and incorporating this into their self-introduction in Korean

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on different ways of communicating and their appropriateness in Korean or non-Korean contexts, for example, using 언니 / 누나 and 오빠 / 형 for older siblings in Korean compared with using their given names in English as terms of address

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing ideas about how some Australian terms and expressions might be understood or confusing from a Korean perspective, such as ‘bushwalking’ or ‘kick a footy’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming aware of the variety of gender-inclusive ways in which people can be addressed, including the use of non-gendered expressions such as 그 사람, 그, or 그 분 (honorific) which can apply to all Korean speakers, and if the name is known, referring to them by their name with the suffix 씨 where appropriate

as_extracts.name: LKORF104-E08
as_extracts.description: They identify patterns in Korean and make comparisons between Korean and English, using simple metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4C04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: develop strategies to comprehend and produce Korean, adjusting language to convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing bilingual word lists or flashcards by identifying known Korean words or expressions and relating them to English equivalents and vice versa, noticing that direct translation sometimes cannot be achieved

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing photos of people interacting and predicting the dialogue in English and in Korean, identifying what would be similar and/or different between the 2 languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating appropriately in familiar situations such as greetings or self-introductions, and identifying the different uses of language in specific contexts, for example, using polite formal forms 저는 민수예요 and 네 with the teacher; using informal forms 나는 민수야 and 응 with peers

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating Korean texts such as 노크하세요, understanding how meaning changes when translated into English and how some Korean expressions demonstrate cultural differences

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discovering individual words and expressions that may be interpreted differently by people who do not know Korean culture, for example, 우리 집, 우리 선생님

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching interactions in Korean and identifying appropriate gestures that accompany language, for example, passing objects with both hands to show respect to a teacher or other adults and elders

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words that change their meaning such as 집 (home/house), depending on context, for example, 집에 가요 (I’m going home) as opposed to 우리 집이에요 (This is our house)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring adjectives and descriptions in Korean and English for familiar topics, identifying words with similarities or differences in meaning between the 2 languages, for example, a description about a friend 수미는 착해요. ; 착한 아이예요. meaning ‘kind’ in English and ‘good, nice, helpful and kind’ in Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on contexts where cultural elements are embedded in language use in Korean, for example, bowing when saying 안녕하세요? and comparing this with equivalent contexts and ways of using verbal and non-verbal language in English and/or other languages

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4U01 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising reading and pronouncing combinations of Hangeul vowels and consonants using chants, songs and language games, for example, bingo, tic tac toe

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between sounds in Korean, especially the ‘tense’ and ‘soft’ sounds, for example, 가 / 카 / 까, 다 / 타 / 따, 바 / 파 / 빠, 사 / 싸, 자 / 차 / 짜, 내 / 네, 너 / 노

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on a piece of paper or mini whiteboards the shape the mouth makes when pronouncing Korean vowels and recognising the similarities of the mouth shapes and Hangeul for each vowel, for example, ㅡ sounds that make the mouth shape flat and long

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating modelled intonation, for example, using rising intonation at the end of a question and lowered intonation to answer (e.g. 학생이에요? 네, 학생이에요. ; 어디 가요? 학교에 가요. ; 피곤해요? 아니요, 괜찮아요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying how pronunciation and intonation are used in spoken, written and multimodal texts to clarify the function of the same word in an interaction or a sentence, for example, 좋아요. ; 아주 좋아요. ; 좋아요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with Hangeul vowels and consonants to construct and deconstruct a Hangeul syllable block using Hangeul cards or blocks, for example, ㅊ + ㅏ = 차 ; ㄱ + ㅏ + ㅇ = 강 ; ㅅ + ㅜ = 수 ; ㄱ + ㅗ + ㅁ = 곰

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some consonants are pronounced differently depending on where they are located in a word, for example, ㅅ in 사랑 is pronounced as ‘s’; ㅅ in 곳 is pronounced as ‘t’

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4U03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise and compare familiar Korean language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using simple metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing language features typically associated with particular texts, for example, the use of imperatives in games such as 주사위를 던져요 and 말을 움직여요

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising Korean in texts such as signage and product labels, and producing their equivalents in English and/or other languages, for example, making an English version of a Korean food product label and emphasising important information such as spice level

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the importance of politeness being explicitly expressed in Korean and comparing this with English and/or other languages, for example, 만나서 반가워요 as opposed to ‘Nice to meet you’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing to practise answering negative questions by agreeing or disagreeing, for example, 안 했어요? 네, 안 했어요. / 아니요, 했어요. ; 밥 안 먹었어요? 네, 안 먹었어요. / 아니요, 먹었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding different aspects of Korean, English and/or other languages and culture such as naming conventions, and explaining differences in word order and spacing, for example, 박준호 as opposed to ‘John Smith’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a short video clip and identifying non-verbal expressions that are typical or expected in communication in different cultures, for example, making or avoiding eye contact, bowing, nodding, pointing

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing parts of a sentence using metalanguage (e.g. noun, verb, adverb, adjective) to describe words, and noticing the word order and patterns

as_extracts.name: LKORF104-E09
as_extracts.description: They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4U04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: identify connections between personal identity, language and aspects of culture
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing a map that shows Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages, noticing how many languages are represented in Victoria, and then learning about the diversity of languages to which students in the classroom have a connection

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place on which they live and incorporating this into their self-introduction in Korean

elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on different ways of communicating and their appropriateness in Korean or non-Korean contexts, for example, using 언니 / 누나 and 오빠 / 형 for older siblings in Korean compared with using their given names in English as terms of address

elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing ideas about how some Australian terms and expressions might be understood or confusing from a Korean perspective, such as ‘bushwalking’ or ‘kick a footy’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming aware of the variety of gender-inclusive ways in which people can be addressed, including the use of non-gendered expressions such as 그 사람, 그, or 그 분 (honorific) which can apply to all Korean speakers, and if the name is known, referring to them by their name with the suffix 씨 where appropriate

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4C01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate exchanges and respond to modelled questions about themselves, others and the classroom environment, using formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple descriptive language and supporting resources to introduce family members and friends such as identifying relationships (e.g. 우리 엄마예요, 친구예요) or cultural backgrounds (e.g. 호주 사람이에요, 한국 사람이에요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of particular occasions, situations or times of day, and deciding which greetings and expressions would be appropriate for the situation or role-playing an interaction in that scenario

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning common ways to join and maintain a conversation, such as asking a question (e.g. 질문 있어요) and requesting repetition (e.g. 다시 말해주세요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: initiating conversation through questions while playing social bingo or other ice-breaker games, for example, 이름이 뭐예요? ;몇 살이에요? ; 뭐 제일 좋아해요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising responses to everyday questions, for example, selecting random questions written on icy pole sticks or generated by a digital program and replying to them using a variety of answers

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in real or simulated situations such as borrowing and lending stationery items using simple Korean expressions, for example, 지우개 있어요? 아니요, 없어요. ; 연필 빌려 주세요. 네, 여기 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging simple correspondence such as notes, invitations or birthday cards in print or secure digital form (mock text messages), for example, 누가 생일 파티에 와요? 제니요. ; 언제 파티해요? 내일 해요.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4C02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve expressing interests and exchanging information, using a range of familiar phrases and modelled structures

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: engaging in conversations with peers in group activities, for example, taking turns to ask questions in number or word guessing games (e.g. 몇이에요? ; 숫자 뭐예요? ; 이게 뭐예요? ; 저게 뭐예요?) and giving simple answers (e.g. 사예요 ; 삼이에요 ; 의자예요 ; 책상이에요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in shared activities such as games, role-plays and chants/rhymes, for example, students taking turns role-playing the teacher and giving classroom commands

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in shared or group reading, taking turns to read, and discussing questions about the content

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making matching cards or digital games to play with peers, using Korean and English words or images regarding topics such as days of the week, months, seasons or vocabulary associated with weather, for example, 여름 (summer), 더워요 (it is hot), 수영복 (swimsuit)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions given in Korean (e.g. 해 보세요, 들으세요, 쓰세요, 말하세요, 읽으세요) to complete a task such as making a craft item with peers

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collaborating and contributing to presentations such as developing part of a presentation of a Korean item for a class show-and-tell, or creating part of a digital presentation about some aspects of a significant cultural event or celebration, for example, 태극기, 설날 음식, 설날 놀이

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: complimenting and encouraging peers while planning an activity, for example, 맞아요. ; 아주 잘했어요. ; 좋은 생각이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a class profile with information collected from peers, for example, creating a chart or database to identify favourite sports, foods or colours

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: praising each other (e.g. (아주) 잘했어요) when working collaboratively with the class on tasks that require following instructions, for example, cooking or other step-based activities such as crafts or drawing tasks

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4C03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate and respond to key information related to familiar content obtained from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to short spoken texts and identifying key information based on context such as identifying the patient’s name, age and symptoms in a hospital role-play containing some unfamiliar language, for example, 자, 앉으세요. 이름이 뭐예요? 유미예요. ; 몇 살이에요? 10 살이에요. ; 어디 아파요? 배가 아파요. ; 뭐 먹었어요? 어제 아이스크림을 많이 먹었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling and reporting information such as surveying peers and making a shared class graph to identify favourite sports, foods or colours, for example, 안나는 피자를 좋아해요. ; 마크는 비빔밥을 좋아해요. ; 아루나는 피자를 좋아해요. ; 피자가 제일 인기 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information about a topic from various sources of spoken, written, viewed and/or multimodal texts, including online resources such as interviews, surveys or brochures, and answering interview questions about the topic

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning that Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples used symbols to record stories and thinking about how Koreans would have used viewed language, such as symbols, to represent objects or stories before the invention of Hangeul

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: obtaining and using factual information from spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts related to other learning areas to gather information related to a topic, for example, reading or watching video clips about a science experiment method; looking at maps for geography; viewing old paintings for art

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and listening to stories or texts and responding by playing silent mime games to represent key characters or vocabulary in the story using body language

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing segments of television programs or a role-play of everyday interactions without sound and identifying or guessing what is happening by focusing on movement and gestures, for example, watching an apology, then identifying and practising the matching body language

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing texts such as traditional Korean tales (e.g. ‘호랑이와 곶감’ or ‘흥부와 놀부’) in different formats, including digital texts, and giving a personal response in Korean language, for example, 무서웠어요. ; 정말 재미있었어요. ; 또 얘기해주세요. ; 저도 곶감 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C03-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing stories and responding to questions about characters, ideas and events, for example, illustrating and captioning aspects of the texts

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C04-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on contexts where cultural elements are embedded in language use in Korean, for example, bowing when saying 안녕하세요? and comparing this with equivalent contexts and ways of using verbal and non-verbal language in English and/or other languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4C05 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts using formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting information on topics of possible interest to similar-aged Korean-speaking peers, for example, creating a multimodal presentation about popular sports or pets in Australia

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating individual texts such as comics, diary entries and short stories, using modelled language to express their own ideas and real or imagined experience (e.g. developing a comic with Korean language dialogue about going shopping to buy a friend’s birthday gift), creating and illustrating short informative texts (e.g. creating a caption for a hand-drawn picture, 우리 집 강아지는 갈색이고 귀여워요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple descriptions of geographical characteristics or places of cultural significance in Korean and matching them to known Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Country or Place locations in their local area or elsewhere in Australia

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a personal profile introducing themselves using spoken or written forms of Korean language to identify their role(s) or membership(s) in groups such as friends, family, class and school, accompanied with illustrations using appropriate labels, for example, 친구, 우리 가족, 우리 반, 우리 학교

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing alternative versions of stories or action songs, using voice, rhythm and gestures to animate characters, or using drawings or story maps to create visual context, for example, changing the ending of ‘호랑이와 곶감’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing and presenting picture/digital books or short scripted plays or animations that use favourite Korean words and expressions, for example, 우와, 정말 최고예요. ; 정말 싫어요. ; 진짜?

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing, modifying and completing their own versions of skits, chants and songs with teacher guidance and scaffolding, for example, reinventing the Possum Magic book as Tiger Magic; telling the story of a real or imagined trip around Korea

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing simple written and multimodal correspondence (e.g. invitations, greeting cards) in print, such as writing a Parents’ Day card incorporating formulaic expressions, simple phrases and sentences, and modelled textual conventions, for example, 엄마 아빠 사랑해요. ; 감사해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying differences between written and spoken texts, for example, comparing a written Korean folktale such as ‘심청전’ with a spoken or sung version

elaborations.name: VC2LK4C05-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing how texts within the same mode can differ, such as a birthday card and a set of instructions for a game on a card

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK4U01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise sound combinations, and use patterns of pronunciation and intonation to form words, phrases and simple sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising reading and pronouncing combinations of Hangeul vowels and consonants using chants, songs and language games, for example, bingo, tic tac toe

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between sounds in Korean, especially the ‘tense’ and ‘soft’ sounds, for example, 가 / 카 / 까, 다 / 타 / 따, 바 / 파 / 빠, 사 / 싸, 자 / 차 / 짜, 내 / 네, 너 / 노

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: drawing on a piece of paper or mini whiteboards the shape the mouth makes when pronouncing Korean vowels and recognising the similarities of the mouth shapes and Hangeul for each vowel, for example, ㅡ sounds that make the mouth shape flat and long

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: imitating modelled intonation, for example, using rising intonation at the end of a question and lowered intonation to answer (e.g. 학생이에요? 네, 학생이에요. ; 어디 가요? 학교에 가요. ; 피곤해요? 아니요, 괜찮아요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying how pronunciation and intonation are used in spoken, written and multimodal texts to clarify the function of the same word in an interaction or a sentence, for example, 좋아요. ; 아주 좋아요. ; 좋아요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with Hangeul vowels and consonants to construct and deconstruct a Hangeul syllable block using Hangeul cards or blocks, for example, ㅊ + ㅏ = 차 ; ㄱ + ㅏ + ㅇ = 강 ; ㅅ + ㅜ = 수 ; ㄱ + ㅗ + ㅁ = 곰

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U01-E07 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E01 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E02 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E03 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E04 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E05 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E06 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E07 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E08 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U02-E11 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E02 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the importance of politeness being explicitly expressed in Korean and comparing this with English and/or other languages, for example, 만나서 반가워요 as opposed to ‘Nice to meet you’

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: role-playing to practise answering negative questions by agreeing or disagreeing, for example, 안 했어요? 네, 안 했어요. / 아니요, 했어요. ; 밥 안 먹었어요? 네, 안 먹었어요. / 아니요, 먹었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK4U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding different aspects of Korean, English and/or other languages and culture such as naming conventions, and explaining differences in word order and spacing, for example, 박준호 as opposed to ‘John Smith’

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 5 and 6, Korean language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences with language. Students communicate and work in collaboration with their peers and teachers in purposeful, creative and structured activities that involve listening, speaking, reading, writing and viewing. They interact in Korean to exchange information and ideas within their school and local environment, and engage with Korean-speaking communities. They work independently and in groups, with ongoing support from modelling and from digital and print resources. 

Students engage with a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts that may include stories, posters, images, notes, invitations, video clips and procedural texts. They identify language structures and features of Korean, and use simple metalanguage to reflect on their understanding. They use their knowledge of Hangeul to obtain meaning from texts. They recognise that some words and expressions are not easily translated, and reflect on how diverse cultural practices, behaviours and values influence communication and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 6, students initiate and use strategies to maintain interactions in Korean that are related to their immediate environment. They use appropriate sound combinations, stress, intonation and rhythm in spoken texts. They collaborate in spoken and written activities to share information, preferences and ideas. They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in Korean or English, adjusting their responses to context, purpose and audience.

Students use modelled structures when creating and responding in Korean. They create texts, selecting and using a variety of vocabulary and sentence structures to suit different contexts. They use conventions appropriate to text type. They apply rules for pronunciation, intonation and stress in spoken language and apply conventions of Hangeul spelling and punctuation in written language. They compare language structures and features in Korean and English, using familiar metalanguage. They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting to exchange information about experiences (e.g. everyday life and leisure activities), using modelled past- and present-tense forms (e.g. giving a presentation about a photo or object during show-and-tell using some formulaic phrases), for example, -해요 / -했어요 ; 오늘 한국어를 공부해요. ; 어제 영어를 공부했어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using communication strategies such as active listening skills and turn-taking cues to support the exchange of ideas and information, for example, supporting a conversation using appropriate filler words

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing likes and dislikes such as 저도 -아 / 어요 and 저도 -았 / 었어요, and providing reasons for opinions using 왜요? and 왜냐하면, for example, 저도 좋아요 ; 저도 좋았어요 ; 저도 축구해요;저도 요리했어요 ; 왜요? 왜냐하면 재미있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E04 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E05 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and expressing concern or sympathy to friends and family members, for example, 괜찮아요? ; 정말 안 됐어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching Korean television shows to identify Korean people’s reactions such as exclamations and body language to show understanding and interest during interactions, and practising using these in class, for example, 우아! ; 이제 알겠어요! ; 진짜요? ; 좋은데요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and participating in role-plays that replicate everyday situations such as asking for information, purchasing items in a shop, recounting experiences and feelings about everyday life and leisure activities

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C02 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E01 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making collaborative decisions and arrangements using Korean, in traditional Korean games, in person or in a secure online environment, such as playing 윷놀이 by counting using 하나, 둘, ordering using 첫 번째, 두 번째, or numbering using 일, 이, …

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to feedback to improve a draft, for example, asking for clarification and adding ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing bilingual texts such as posters, for class or school assembly performances, events or displays, for example, 스승의 날, 어버이날

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E06 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying reading skills by chunking the phrases in a sentence, for example, recognising the time expression 오늘 오후 세 시에 in 저는 오늘 오후 세 시에 친구하고 수영해요 as a chunk

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the Korean computer keyboard system and recognising its patterns (e.g. all Korean vowels are located on the right side of the keyboard), and experimenting with typing out words, with support

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E03 - Korean
