as_extracts.description: They use strategies to locate and interpret information and ideas in texts, and demonstrate understanding by responding in Korean or English, adjusting their responses to context, purpose and audience.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of different Korean primary school classroom environments (e.g. classrooms for different subjects) and using a ‘see-think-wonder’ thinking routine to reflect on the image, then discussing the similarities and differences between a Korean classroom and their Australian classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing subtitled video clips of Korean-speaking people conversing, and identifying new language such as interjections, to record and use with peers, for example, 우와! ; 말도 안 돼! ; 농담하지 마!

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching topics such as recycling, the water cycle, the solar system, or geographical features of Korea in English, and organising and sharing the information in Korean, using modelled language in print or digital infographics that use both written and viewed text, for example, pictures of Korean recycling symbols with written instructions for how to recycle

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in different types of texts such as advertisements, conversations, brochures and announcements, and sharing this information with others in another format, for example, presenting a chart of favourite television programs or computer games

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in Korean, for example, 너무 감동적이에요. ; 가장 기억에 남는 장면은 이 장면이예요.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing a variety of texts about concepts related to other learning areas such as the arts, humanities and sciences that Korean students at the same level learn in Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information and discussing the similarities and differences in the topics learnt in Australian and Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing texts such as performances, game shows, music videos and artwork, and sharing opinions or feelings about them using expressions such as 어땠어요? 너무 좋아요. / 너무 좋았어요. ; 정말 재미있어요. / 정말 재미있었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing storyboards to sequence key events in different types of informative or imaginative texts, including captions, subtitles or word bubbles to capture moods or feelings, for example, 무서워요, 행복해요, 이상해요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and comparing perspectives represented in spoken and written informative texts and using formulaic expressions such as 누가 썼어요? ; 누가 말했어요? ; 네 생각에 -이 / 가 맞아요? ; 왜 맞아요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing favourite characters in stories, plays or cartoons, listing words or expressions associated with their personality such as 착해요, 예뻐요, 멋있어요, 무서워요, 이상해요, and explaining how they can relate to them, for example, 저는 -이 / 가 좋아요, 싫어요

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying strategies to communicate with adults (e.g. a teacher), such as verbally agreeing with what they say, nodding and politely declining, for example, 네, 그래요, 맞습니다. ; 아니요, 죄송합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in Korean and English that cannot be readily translated and clarifying meanings for such words by providing examples, explanations or extra information, for example, recognising and explaining the difference between 벼 (rice as a crop), 쌀 (rice as raw grains), 밥 (cooked rice/meals)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, using glossaries or online dictionaries to find examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on diverse interpretations of everyday language use in Korean, for example, the possibility that certain phrases such as 어디 가요? and 밥 먹었어요? can be greetings or genuine questions depending on the context

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of and reflecting on the significance of gestures across cultures, for example, bowing, when to use or avoid eye contact, shaking hands, making a ‘V’ gesture with 2 fingers, putting hands up at restaurants

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding signage from their local area, and interpreting and comparing it to signage in Korea, for example, comparing traffic and road signs or signs in public places

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Korean language is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions, for example, a growing number of English words being borrowed or adopted into Korean such as 핸드폰 for mobile phone, 노트북 for laptop, 아이쇼핑 for window shopping

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: compare some Korean language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key features in specific text types and comparing these with English and/or other languages’ equivalents, for example, the use of –에게 / 께 (to) in salutations and -(으)로부터 / 올림 (from) in closing in a letter, email or invitation

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing text types and language features in Korean, English and/or other languages, for example, comparing a recipe for kimchi fried rice in Korean with a recipe for kimchi fried rice in English

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching Korean loan words to the original words in English and other languages, and exploring their origins, for example, 피아노, 피자, 케밥

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some words originate from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages from different areas around Australia, for example, 코알라 (koala) from the Dharug word gula, meaning ‘no water’, or 캥거루 (kangaroo) from the Guugu Yimithirr word gangarru, and comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying Korean words used in Australia and sharing their own experiences of using or encountering them, for example, 비빔밥, 태권도

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key details, context and intended audience in a range of familiar texts in Korean (e.g. phone messages, sports reports, takeaway food orders), and comparing how this information is presented in Korean texts with how it is presented in English and/or other language texts, for example, comparing a Korean menu and an English menu from the same Korean food restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing feedback to support their peers using metalanguage, for example, editing each other’s written or spoken texts and work samples and justifying their reasons

elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about an imaginary trip to Korea, incorporating some famous places and cultural observations, for example, 금요일에 명동에 갔어요. ; 쇼핑하고 맛있는 길거리 음식을 먹었어요. ; 특별한 시간이었어요.

content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising spacing and spelling rules in reading and writing using drawings or comic strips showing how one wrong spacing can change the whole context of the sentence, for example, 소라가 방에 있어요 compared to 소라 가방에 있어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spacing and spelling rules in Korean with similar rules in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple events occurring in the past in a show-and-tell in front of peers using -었 / 았-, for example, 캔버라에 살았어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the formal polite ending -ㅂ / 습니다 and the casual ending -어 / 아, 해, and understanding the different contexts where different levels of politeness and formality are indicated by verb endings, for example, 미안합니다 compared to 미안해요 compared to 미안해

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing matching games using both counting systems correctly with counter words such as 장, 잔, 권, 그루, 송이, 원, 시, 분, 번째, ... and reading Arabic numerals with the appropriate pronunciation according to the numbering system that is used, for example, 책 3 권 is read as [책 세 권], 10 살 is read as [열 살], 6 학년 is read as [육 학년], 7 시 is read as [일곱 시]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phrases with the noun+particle structure such as –하고, –에서, –(으)로 in a sentence, for example, 친구하고 쇼핑했어요. ; 학교에서 공부해요. ; 펜으로 쓰세요. ; 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 비가 안 와요. ; 김치를 못 먹었어요.), and making a list of actions that fall under 내가 못 하는 것 as opposed to 내가 안 하는 것

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a sequence of events by using conjunctive adverbs (e.g. 그리고) at the beginning of a new sentence, for example, 밥을 먹어요. 그리고 운동을 해요, and using conjunctive suffixes (e.g. -고) in a coordinative structure, for example, using flashcards of action verbs to make one sentence describing sequences of events (e.g. 밥을 먹고 운동을 해요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the complex structures -(으)ㄴ / 는 것 같다 and –도 되다 in the informal polite ending -어 / 아요 to express opinions and give or request permission, for example, 맞는 것 같아요. ; 가도 돼요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how word order and syntactic functions are different in simple sentences in Korean and English, for example, ‘저는 (subject) 사과를 (object) 먹어요 (verb)’ as opposed to ‘I (subject) eat (verb) an apple (object)’, and playing sentence unjumbling games

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying strategies to communicate with adults (e.g. a teacher), such as verbally agreeing with what they say, nodding and politely declining, for example, 네, 그래요, 맞습니다. ; 아니요, 죄송합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in Korean and English that cannot be readily translated and clarifying meanings for such words by providing examples, explanations or extra information, for example, recognising and explaining the difference between 벼 (rice as a crop), 쌀 (rice as raw grains), 밥 (cooked rice/meals)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, using glossaries or online dictionaries to find examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on diverse interpretations of everyday language use in Korean, for example, the possibility that certain phrases such as 어디 가요? and 밥 먹었어요? can be greetings or genuine questions depending on the context

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of and reflecting on the significance of gestures across cultures, for example, bowing, when to use or avoid eye contact, shaking hands, making a ‘V’ gesture with 2 fingers, putting hands up at restaurants

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding signage from their local area, and interpreting and comparing it to signage in Korea, for example, comparing traffic and road signs or signs in public places

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Korean language is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions, for example, a growing number of English words being borrowed or adopted into Korean such as 핸드폰 for mobile phone, 노트북 for laptop, 아이쇼핑 for window shopping

content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, stress, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing written Korean words and practising transitioning smoothly to the following syllables, for example, 한국어 as [한구거]; 같이 as [가치] ; 감사합니다 as [감사함니다]; 먹고 as [먹꼬]; 어떻게 as [어떠케]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that ㅇ is a silent Hangeul and practising carrying the pronunciation over from the previous consonant when ㅇ is present, for example, pronouncing 어린이 as [어리니]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between words with different tonal sounds and meanings (e.g. 이 ‘two’ and 이 ‘tooth’; 밤 ‘chestnut’ and 밤 ‘night’), by composing a tongue twister and practising other students’ tongue twisters

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using rising intonation at the end of a question and responding to it with falling intonation, 학생이에요? 네, 맞아요. / 아니요, 선생님이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying reading skills by chunking the phrases in a sentence, for example, recognising the time expression 오늘 오후 세 시에 in 저는 오늘 오후 세 시에 친구하고 수영해요 as a chunk

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the Korean computer keyboard system and recognising its patterns (e.g. all Korean vowels are located on the right side of the keyboard), and experimenting with typing out words, with support

elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 비가 안 와요. ; 김치를 못 먹었어요.), and making a list of actions that fall under 내가 못 하는 것 as opposed to 내가 안 하는 것

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a sequence of events by using conjunctive adverbs (e.g. 그리고) at the beginning of a new sentence, for example, 밥을 먹어요. 그리고 운동을 해요, and using conjunctive suffixes (e.g. -고) in a coordinative structure, for example, using flashcards of action verbs to make one sentence describing sequences of events (e.g. 밥을 먹고 운동을 해요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the complex structures -(으)ㄴ / 는 것 같다 and –도 되다 in the informal polite ending -어 / 아요 to express opinions and give or request permission, for example, 맞는 것 같아요. ; 가도 돼요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how word order and syntactic functions are different in simple sentences in Korean and English, for example, ‘저는 (subject) 사과를 (object) 먹어요 (verb)’ as opposed to ‘I (subject) eat (verb) an apple (object)’, and playing sentence unjumbling games

as_extracts.name: LKORF106-E08
as_extracts.description: They apply rules for pronunciation, intonation and stress in spoken language and apply conventions of Hangeul spelling and punctuation in written language.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying strategies to communicate with adults (e.g. a teacher), such as verbally agreeing with what they say, nodding and politely declining, for example, 네, 그래요, 맞습니다. ; 아니요, 죄송합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in Korean and English that cannot be readily translated and clarifying meanings for such words by providing examples, explanations or extra information, for example, recognising and explaining the difference between 벼 (rice as a crop), 쌀 (rice as raw grains), 밥 (cooked rice/meals)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, using glossaries or online dictionaries to find examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on diverse interpretations of everyday language use in Korean, for example, the possibility that certain phrases such as 어디 가요? and 밥 먹었어요? can be greetings or genuine questions depending on the context

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of and reflecting on the significance of gestures across cultures, for example, bowing, when to use or avoid eye contact, shaking hands, making a ‘V’ gesture with 2 fingers, putting hands up at restaurants

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding signage from their local area, and interpreting and comparing it to signage in Korea, for example, comparing traffic and road signs or signs in public places

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Korean language is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions, for example, a growing number of English words being borrowed or adopted into Korean such as 핸드폰 for mobile phone, 노트북 for laptop, 아이쇼핑 for window shopping

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C05 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video clip to present information or ideas to a particular audience (e.g. a virtual tour of the school or classroom for exchange student groups), using empathy to consider elements that may be unfamiliar to Korean students, for example, Australian students generally bring lunch to school; schools start at 9am and finish around 3pm

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using calligraphy pens and ink to write sentences about a topic or theme and designing and/or creating a picture to match

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting comparisons between Korea and Australia, for example, population statistics and physical size, daily temperatures, types of housing, pet ownership, popular leisure activities

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a recipe incorporating some typical Korean ingredients, using modelled procedural language, for example, 먼저 오이를 잘라요. ; 그리고 참기름을 넣어요. ; 고추장하고 소금을 넣어요. ; 다 같이 섞어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple picture books to read to younger students to demonstrate the benefits of learning Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about an imaginary trip to Korea, incorporating some famous places and cultural observations, for example, 금요일에 명동에 갔어요. ; 쇼핑하고 맛있는 길거리 음식을 먹었어요. ; 특별한 시간이었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a board game, focusing on key language, and using expressions for playing games such as creating rules, procedures and instructions, for example, 한 칸 더 가요. ; 두 칸 뒤로 가요.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U01 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, stress, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing written Korean words and practising transitioning smoothly to the following syllables, for example, 한국어 as [한구거]; 같이 as [가치] ; 감사합니다 as [감사함니다]; 먹고 as [먹꼬]; 어떻게 as [어떠케]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that ㅇ is a silent Hangeul and practising carrying the pronunciation over from the previous consonant when ㅇ is present, for example, pronouncing 어린이 as [어리니]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between words with different tonal sounds and meanings (e.g. 이 ‘two’ and 이 ‘tooth’; 밤 ‘chestnut’ and 밤 ‘night’), by composing a tongue twister and practising other students’ tongue twisters

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using rising intonation at the end of a question and responding to it with falling intonation, 학생이에요? 네, 맞아요. / 아니요, 선생님이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying reading skills by chunking the phrases in a sentence, for example, recognising the time expression 오늘 오후 세 시에 in 저는 오늘 오후 세 시에 친구하고 수영해요 as a chunk

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the Korean computer keyboard system and recognising its patterns (e.g. all Korean vowels are located on the right side of the keyboard), and experimenting with typing out words, with support

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising spacing and spelling rules in reading and writing using drawings or comic strips showing how one wrong spacing can change the whole context of the sentence, for example, 소라가 방에 있어요 compared to 소라 가방에 있어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spacing and spelling rules in Korean with similar rules in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple events occurring in the past in a show-and-tell in front of peers using -었 / 았-, for example, 캔버라에 살았어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the formal polite ending -ㅂ / 습니다 and the casual ending -어 / 아, 해, and understanding the different contexts where different levels of politeness and formality are indicated by verb endings, for example, 미안합니다 compared to 미안해요 compared to 미안해

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing matching games using both counting systems correctly with counter words such as 장, 잔, 권, 그루, 송이, 원, 시, 분, 번째, ... and reading Arabic numerals with the appropriate pronunciation according to the numbering system that is used, for example, 책 3 권 is read as [책 세 권], 10 살 is read as [열 살], 6 학년 is read as [육 학년], 7 시 is read as [일곱 시]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phrases with the noun+particle structure such as –하고, –에서, –(으)로 in a sentence, for example, 친구하고 쇼핑했어요. ; 학교에서 공부해요. ; 펜으로 쓰세요. ; 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 비가 안 와요. ; 김치를 못 먹었어요.), and making a list of actions that fall under 내가 못 하는 것 as opposed to 내가 안 하는 것

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a sequence of events by using conjunctive adverbs (e.g. 그리고) at the beginning of a new sentence, for example, 밥을 먹어요. 그리고 운동을 해요, and using conjunctive suffixes (e.g. -고) in a coordinative structure, for example, using flashcards of action verbs to make one sentence describing sequences of events (e.g. 밥을 먹고 운동을 해요.)

elaborations.elaboration_text: using the complex structures -(으)ㄴ / 는 것 같다 and –도 되다 in the informal polite ending -어 / 아요 to express opinions and give or request permission, for example, 맞는 것 같아요. ; 가도 돼요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how word order and syntactic functions are different in simple sentences in Korean and English, for example, ‘저는 (subject) 사과를 (object) 먹어요 (verb)’ as opposed to ‘I (subject) eat (verb) an apple (object)’, and playing sentence unjumbling games

as_extracts.description: They compare language structures and features in Korean and English, using familiar metalanguage.

content_descriptions.text: compare some Korean language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key features in specific text types and comparing these with English and/or other languages’ equivalents, for example, the use of –에게 / 께 (to) in salutations and -(으)로부터 / 올림 (from) in closing in a letter, email or invitation

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing text types and language features in Korean, English and/or other languages, for example, comparing a recipe for kimchi fried rice in Korean with a recipe for kimchi fried rice in English

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching Korean loan words to the original words in English and other languages, and exploring their origins, for example, 피아노, 피자, 케밥

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some words originate from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages from different areas around Australia, for example, 코알라 (koala) from the Dharug word gula, meaning ‘no water’, or 캥거루 (kangaroo) from the Guugu Yimithirr word gangarru, and comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying Korean words used in Australia and sharing their own experiences of using or encountering them, for example, 비빔밥, 태권도

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key details, context and intended audience in a range of familiar texts in Korean (e.g. phone messages, sports reports, takeaway food orders), and comparing how this information is presented in Korean texts with how it is presented in English and/or other language texts, for example, comparing a Korean menu and an English menu from the same Korean food restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing feedback to support their peers using metalanguage, for example, editing each other’s written or spoken texts and work samples and justifying their reasons

as_extracts.name: LKORF106-E10
as_extracts.description: They show understanding of how language and culture are interconnected and consider how this is reflected in their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of different Korean primary school classroom environments (e.g. classrooms for different subjects) and using a ‘see-think-wonder’ thinking routine to reflect on the image, then discussing the similarities and differences between a Korean classroom and their Australian classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing subtitled video clips of Korean-speaking people conversing, and identifying new language such as interjections, to record and use with peers, for example, 우와! ; 말도 안 돼! ; 농담하지 마!

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching topics such as recycling, the water cycle, the solar system, or geographical features of Korea in English, and organising and sharing the information in Korean, using modelled language in print or digital infographics that use both written and viewed text, for example, pictures of Korean recycling symbols with written instructions for how to recycle

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in different types of texts such as advertisements, conversations, brochures and announcements, and sharing this information with others in another format, for example, presenting a chart of favourite television programs or computer games

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in Korean, for example, 너무 감동적이에요. ; 가장 기억에 남는 장면은 이 장면이예요.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing a variety of texts about concepts related to other learning areas such as the arts, humanities and sciences that Korean students at the same level learn in Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information and discussing the similarities and differences in the topics learnt in Australian and Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing texts such as performances, game shows, music videos and artwork, and sharing opinions or feelings about them using expressions such as 어땠어요? 너무 좋아요. / 너무 좋았어요. ; 정말 재미있어요. / 정말 재미있었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing storyboards to sequence key events in different types of informative or imaginative texts, including captions, subtitles or word bubbles to capture moods or feelings, for example, 무서워요, 행복해요, 이상해요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and comparing perspectives represented in spoken and written informative texts and using formulaic expressions such as 누가 썼어요? ; 누가 말했어요? ; 네 생각에 -이 / 가 맞아요? ; 왜 맞아요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing favourite characters in stories, plays or cartoons, listing words or expressions associated with their personality such as 착해요, 예뻐요, 멋있어요, 무서워요, 이상해요, and explaining how they can relate to them, for example, 저는 -이 / 가 좋아요, 싫어요

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this has an impact on verbal and non-verbal communication
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the significance of some social conventions and cultural concepts that young people follow in Korean-speaking communities, for example, 잘 먹겠습니다. ; 잘 먹었습니다. ; 학교 잘 다녀오겠습니다. ; 학교 잘 다녀왔습니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and exploring cultural aspects embedded in or accompanying language use, such as the use of honorifics and different terms of address (e.g. identifying the change in tone and volume of the person’s voice when they speak using honorifics as opposed to informal casual language), and discussing how it can show respect

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching or experiencing traditional Korean celebrations such as 설날 and learning about associated practices (e.g. 윷놀이, 한복, 떡국, 사물놀이), commenting on the experience with descriptions and recommendations (e.g. 한복이 멋있어요. ; 한복을 입어 보세요. ; 사물놀이가 흥겨워요.), and making connections to or comparisons with their own culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on, in Korean or English, how language and culture are expressed through Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander songs, dances or artworks, considering similarities and differences in an aspect of the cultural expressions of Korean-speaking people or communities

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing stories about the creation of Hangeul, such as stories about 세종대왕, and reflecting on the background or rationale for the creation of Hangeul

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring examples of traditional and contemporary images or texts in print and online, and discussing how identity and gender are represented in the language

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing traditional methods that Korean speakers use to preserve language and culture; comparing these with examples of cultural artefacts such as dances, songs, artworks, artefacts or traditions, from a range of different cultures; and identifying how they strengthen connections to values and identity, for example, discussing the significance of a possum-skin coat for some Aboriginal Peoples and sharing similarities and differences between cultural artefacts in other languages and cultures represented in the classroom

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

substrand_content_descriptions.text: initiate and sustain modelled exchanges in familiar contexts related to their personal worlds and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting to exchange information about experiences (e.g. everyday life and leisure activities), using modelled past- and present-tense forms (e.g. giving a presentation about a photo or object during show-and-tell using some formulaic phrases), for example, -해요 / -했어요 ; 오늘 한국어를 공부해요. ; 어제 영어를 공부했어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using communication strategies such as active listening skills and turn-taking cues to support the exchange of ideas and information, for example, supporting a conversation using appropriate filler words

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing likes and dislikes such as 저도 -아 / 어요 and 저도 -았 / 었어요, and providing reasons for opinions using 왜요? and 왜냐하면, for example, 저도 좋아요 ; 저도 좋았어요 ; 저도 축구해요;저도 요리했어요 ; 왜요? 왜냐하면 재미있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recounting and comparing experiences with family and friends in spoken and written forms such as conversations, diaries or simulated blogs, for example, 토요일에 저는 친구하고 쇼핑했어요. ; 제니하고 시내에 갔어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: communicating using a secure, teacher-moderated online environment with Korean-speaking peers living in Korea, using communication strategies such as active listening skills, turn-taking cues and requests for clarification or more detail to support interactions, for example, 미안해요. ; 하지만 잘 몰라요. ; 무슨 말이에요? ; 다시 말해 줘요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: apologising and expressing concern or sympathy to friends and family members, for example, 괜찮아요? ; 정말 안 됐어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching Korean television shows to identify Korean people’s reactions such as exclamations and body language to show understanding and interest during interactions, and practising using these in class, for example, 우아! ; 이제 알겠어요! ; 진짜요? ; 좋은데요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C01-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and participating in role-plays that replicate everyday situations such as asking for information, purchasing items in a shop, recounting experiences and feelings about everyday life and leisure activities

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: participate in activities that involve discussion with others, using language that expresses information, preferences and ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in an activity for a school assembly, school or class event or performance, using language related to place, people, items, time or numbers and creating promotional materials, for example, producing a poster or video to encourage recycling (e.g. 플라스틱을 학교에 가져 오지 말아요. ; 어디에 이거 넣어요?)

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a questionnaire to create a spotlight or profile of a fellow student or teacher and then recording the interview as a video or a written article for the school newspaper or website

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: making collaborative decisions and arrangements using Korean, in traditional Korean games, in person or in a secure online environment, such as playing 윷놀이 by counting using 하나, 둘, ordering using 첫 번째, 두 번째, or numbering using 일, 이, …

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: responding to feedback to improve a draft, for example, asking for clarification and adding ideas

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing bilingual texts such as posters, for class or school assembly performances, events or displays, for example, 스승의 날, 어버이날

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking peers to do something and responding to requests (e.g. 더 크게 말해줘요 ; 다시 말해줘요), or giving instructions for peers to follow by miming the activities, for example, 한복 입어요. ; 쇼핑 가요. ; 김치 먹어요!

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating and performing role-plays simulating simple transactions involving asking for or giving prices, or asking for goods or services, for example, 얼마예요? 오천 원이에요. ; 아이스크림 한 개 주세요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: allocating and swapping roles in group activities, for example, 내 차례야. ; 제 차례예요. ; 네 차례가 아니야. ; ... 씨 차례예요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and creating shared class rules and procedures, including advice and reminders, for example, 빨리 해요 ; 천천히 해요 ; 숙제했어요?

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Mediating meaning in and between languages
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Mediating meaning in and between languages

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, and respond in different ways to suit purpose
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing images of different Korean primary school classroom environments (e.g. classrooms for different subjects) and using a ‘see-think-wonder’ thinking routine to reflect on the image, then discussing the similarities and differences between a Korean classroom and their Australian classroom

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing subtitled video clips of Korean-speaking people conversing, and identifying new language such as interjections, to record and use with peers, for example, 우와! ; 말도 안 돼! ; 농담하지 마!

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching topics such as recycling, the water cycle, the solar system, or geographical features of Korea in English, and organising and sharing the information in Korean, using modelled language in print or digital infographics that use both written and viewed text, for example, pictures of Korean recycling symbols with written instructions for how to recycle

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying information in different types of texts such as advertisements, conversations, brochures and announcements, and sharing this information with others in another format, for example, presenting a chart of favourite television programs or computer games

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them using words, formulaic expressions and modelled sentences in Korean, for example, 너무 감동적이에요. ; 가장 기억에 남는 장면은 이 장면이예요.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading and viewing a variety of texts about concepts related to other learning areas such as the arts, humanities and sciences that Korean students at the same level learn in Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting information and discussing the similarities and differences in the topics learnt in Australian and Korean schools

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing texts such as performances, game shows, music videos and artwork, and sharing opinions or feelings about them using expressions such as 어땠어요? 너무 좋아요. / 너무 좋았어요. ; 정말 재미있어요. / 정말 재미있었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing storyboards to sequence key events in different types of informative or imaginative texts, including captions, subtitles or word bubbles to capture moods or feelings, for example, 무서워요, 행복해요, 이상해요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and comparing perspectives represented in spoken and written informative texts and using formulaic expressions such as 누가 썼어요? ; 누가 말했어요? ; 네 생각에 -이 / 가 맞아요? ; 왜 맞아요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C03-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing favourite characters in stories, plays or cartoons, listing words or expressions associated with their personality such as 착해요, 예뻐요, 멋있어요, 무서워요, 이상해요, and explaining how they can relate to them, for example, 저는 -이 / 가 좋아요, 싫어요

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C04 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply strategies to interpret and convey meaning and/or intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar non-verbal, spoken and written contexts
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying strategies to communicate with adults (e.g. a teacher), such as verbally agreeing with what they say, nodding and politely declining, for example, 네, 그래요, 맞습니다. ; 아니요, 죄송합니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words in Korean and English that cannot be readily translated and clarifying meanings for such words by providing examples, explanations or extra information, for example, recognising and explaining the difference between 벼 (rice as a crop), 쌀 (rice as raw grains), 밥 (cooked rice/meals)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual resources for language learning, for example, using glossaries or online dictionaries to find examples and explanations of parts of speech and language use

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on diverse interpretations of everyday language use in Korean, for example, the possibility that certain phrases such as 어디 가요? and 밥 먹었어요? can be greetings or genuine questions depending on the context

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding examples of and reflecting on the significance of gestures across cultures, for example, bowing, when to use or avoid eye contact, shaking hands, making a ‘V’ gesture with 2 fingers, putting hands up at restaurants

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding signage from their local area, and interpreting and comparing it to signage in Korea, for example, comparing traffic and road signs or signs in public places

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Korean language is constantly expanding to include new words and expressions, for example, a growing number of English words being borrowed or adopted into Korean such as 핸드폰 for mobile phone, 노트북 for laptop, 아이쇼핑 for window shopping

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6C05 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create and present spoken and written texts, using a variety of vocabulary, modelled sentence structures and conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a video clip to present information or ideas to a particular audience (e.g. a virtual tour of the school or classroom for exchange student groups), using empathy to consider elements that may be unfamiliar to Korean students, for example, Australian students generally bring lunch to school; schools start at 9am and finish around 3pm

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using calligraphy pens and ink to write sentences about a topic or theme and designing and/or creating a picture to match

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: presenting comparisons between Korea and Australia, for example, population statistics and physical size, daily temperatures, types of housing, pet ownership, popular leisure activities

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a recipe incorporating some typical Korean ingredients, using modelled procedural language, for example, 먼저 오이를 잘라요. ; 그리고 참기름을 넣어요. ; 고추장하고 소금을 넣어요. ; 다 같이 섞어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating simple picture books to read to younger students to demonstrate the benefits of learning Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recording a multimedia presentation or writing a diary about an imaginary trip to Korea, incorporating some famous places and cultural observations, for example, 금요일에 명동에 갔어요. ; 쇼핑하고 맛있는 길거리 음식을 먹었어요. ; 특별한 시간이었어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6C05-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a board game, focusing on key language, and using expressions for playing games such as creating rules, procedures and instructions, for example, 한 칸 더 가요. ; 두 칸 뒤로 가요.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: apply combinations of sounds, syllables, stress, pronunciation and intonation patterns to develop fluency in words, phrases and sentences

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: pronouncing written Korean words and practising transitioning smoothly to the following syllables, for example, 한국어 as [한구거]; 같이 as [가치] ; 감사합니다 as [감사함니다]; 먹고 as [먹꼬]; 어떻게 as [어떠케]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that ㅇ is a silent Hangeul and practising carrying the pronunciation over from the previous consonant when ㅇ is present, for example, pronouncing 어린이 as [어리니]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between words with different tonal sounds and meanings (e.g. 이 ‘two’ and 이 ‘tooth’; 밤 ‘chestnut’ and 밤 ‘night’), by composing a tongue twister and practising other students’ tongue twisters

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using rising intonation at the end of a question and responding to it with falling intonation, 학생이에요? 네, 맞아요. / 아니요, 선생님이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying reading skills by chunking the phrases in a sentence, for example, recognising the time expression 오늘 오후 세 시에 in 저는 오늘 오후 세 시에 친구하고 수영해요 as a chunk

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: examining the Korean computer keyboard system and recognising its patterns (e.g. all Korean vowels are located on the right side of the keyboard), and experimenting with typing out words, with support

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use a range of modelled grammatical structures to respond to and create simple texts using conventions appropriate to text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising spacing and spelling rules in reading and writing using drawings or comic strips showing how one wrong spacing can change the whole context of the sentence, for example, 소라가 방에 있어요 compared to 소라 가방에 있어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing spacing and spelling rules in Korean with similar rules in English and/or other languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing simple events occurring in the past in a show-and-tell in front of peers using -었 / 았-, for example, 캔버라에 살았어요

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the formal polite ending -ㅂ / 습니다 and the casual ending -어 / 아, 해, and understanding the different contexts where different levels of politeness and formality are indicated by verb endings, for example, 미안합니다 compared to 미안해요 compared to 미안해

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: playing matching games using both counting systems correctly with counter words such as 장, 잔, 권, 그루, 송이, 원, 시, 분, 번째, ... and reading Arabic numerals with the appropriate pronunciation according to the numbering system that is used, for example, 책 3 권 is read as [책 세 권], 10 살 is read as [열 살], 6 학년 is read as [육 학년], 7 시 is read as [일곱 시]

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using phrases with the noun+particle structure such as –하고, –에서, –(으)로 in a sentence, for example, 친구하고 쇼핑했어요. ; 학교에서 공부해요. ; 펜으로 쓰세요. ; 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 비가 안 와요. ; 김치를 못 먹었어요.), and making a list of actions that fall under 내가 못 하는 것 as opposed to 내가 안 하는 것

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a sequence of events by using conjunctive adverbs (e.g. 그리고) at the beginning of a new sentence, for example, 밥을 먹어요. 그리고 운동을 해요, and using conjunctive suffixes (e.g. -고) in a coordinative structure, for example, using flashcards of action verbs to make one sentence describing sequences of events (e.g. 밥을 먹고 운동을 해요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the complex structures -(으)ㄴ / 는 것 같다 and –도 되다 in the informal polite ending -어 / 아요 to express opinions and give or request permission, for example, 맞는 것 같아요. ; 가도 돼요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how word order and syntactic functions are different in simple sentences in Korean and English, for example, ‘저는 (subject) 사과를 (object) 먹어요 (verb)’ as opposed to ‘I (subject) eat (verb) an apple (object)’, and playing sentence unjumbling games

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: compare some Korean language structures and features with those of English and/or other languages, using familiar metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key features in specific text types and comparing these with English and/or other languages’ equivalents, for example, the use of –에게 / 께 (to) in salutations and -(으)로부터 / 올림 (from) in closing in a letter, email or invitation

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing text types and language features in Korean, English and/or other languages, for example, comparing a recipe for kimchi fried rice in Korean with a recipe for kimchi fried rice in English

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching Korean loan words to the original words in English and other languages, and exploring their origins, for example, 피아노, 피자, 케밥

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that some words originate from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander languages from different areas around Australia, for example, 코알라 (koala) from the Dharug word gula, meaning ‘no water’, or 캥거루 (kangaroo) from the Guugu Yimithirr word gangarru, and comparing these words to English and/or other languages and discussing their historical context

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying Korean words used in Australia and sharing their own experiences of using or encountering them, for example, 비빔밥, 태권도

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying key details, context and intended audience in a range of familiar texts in Korean (e.g. phone messages, sports reports, takeaway food orders), and comparing how this information is presented in Korean texts with how it is presented in English and/or other language texts, for example, comparing a Korean menu and an English menu from the same Korean food restaurant

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: providing feedback to support their peers using metalanguage, for example, editing each other’s written or spoken texts and work samples and justifying their reasons

strand_substrands.substrand_title: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture
strand_substrands.substrand_tag: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK6U04 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: recognise that language reflects cultural practices, values and identity, and that this has an impact on verbal and non-verbal communication
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the significance of some social conventions and cultural concepts that young people follow in Korean-speaking communities, for example, 잘 먹겠습니다. ; 잘 먹었습니다. ; 학교 잘 다녀오겠습니다. ; 학교 잘 다녀왔습니다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and exploring cultural aspects embedded in or accompanying language use, such as the use of honorifics and different terms of address (e.g. identifying the change in tone and volume of the person’s voice when they speak using honorifics as opposed to informal casual language), and discussing how it can show respect

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching or experiencing traditional Korean celebrations such as 설날 and learning about associated practices (e.g. 윷놀이, 한복, 떡국, 사물놀이), commenting on the experience with descriptions and recommendations (e.g. 한복이 멋있어요. ; 한복을 입어 보세요. ; 사물놀이가 흥겨워요.), and making connections to or comparisons with their own culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on, in Korean or English, how language and culture are expressed through Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander songs, dances or artworks, considering similarities and differences in an aspect of the cultural expressions of Korean-speaking people or communities

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK2
organising_ideas.text: The interrelationships between people and the diverse environments and systems across the Asia region have global implications.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK6U04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing stories about the creation of Hangeul, such as stories about 세종대왕, and reflecting on the background or rationale for the creation of Hangeul

curriculum_band_description.body:
In Levels 7 and 8, Korean language learning builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students use Korean to interact and collaborate, in person or virtually, within and beyond the classroom. They listen, speak, read, write and view to exchange information, ideas and opinions about their world. They work independently and in groups, and continue to receive feedback and support from their peers and teachers.  

Students access a range of spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts from a variety of authentic sources, which may include audio and video clips, magazines, advertisements, images, stories and articles. They use their knowledge of metalanguage in an increasing range of contexts to reflect on similarities and differences between Korean, English and/or other language structures and features. They recognise that language choices reflect cultural values, beliefs and identity.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 8, students initiate and maintain Korean-language interactions in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts related to a range of interests and experiences. They use Korean to collaborate and problem-solve, and adjust their language in response to others. They interpret information, ideas and opinions in texts. They demonstrate understanding of the similarities and differences between languages, in both familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, by adjusting and reorganising responses. They sequence information and ideas, and select and use vocabulary, sentence structures and expressions to create texts appropriate to context, purpose and audience.

Students apply the conventions of spoken Korean and continue to enhance their fluency. They demonstrate understanding that spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts use different conventions, structures and features to convey meaning. They comment on structures and features of Korean text, using some metalanguage. They reflect on how the Korean language, culture and identity are interconnected, and compare this with their own language(s), culture(s) and identity.
