content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of Hangeul and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing syllable blocks in different shapes, where a consonant and a vertical vowel are positioned side by side (e.g. 가), a horizontal vowel is positioned underneath a consonant (e.g. 누), or a consonant or a consonant cluster is added as a syllable-final consonant (e.g. 받침), under the first 2 types of syllable blocks, for example, 각, 눈, 닭

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining syllable blocks to write a word and applying spacing rules and basic phonological rules when reading and writing, for example, 친구가 교실에서 책을 읽어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple sentence structures in the ‘subject + object + verb’ order to make statements or ask questions, and inferring missing subjects or objects based on context, for example, 지금 무엇을 해요? is missing a subject, and 먹어요 is missing both a subject and an object

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to self and things appropriately using first-person pronouns 저, 제, 나, 내, 우리, demonstrative pronouns 이, 그, 저, 이것, 그것, 저것, or place pronouns 여기, 거기, 저기, for example, 이 사과가 맛있어요. ; 이것이 영어로 뭐예요? ; 여기가 우리 집이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic particles to mark case and other basic functions of nouns in a sentence, for example, -이 / 가, -을 / 를, -은 / 는, -에, -에서, -하고

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using present and past tenses with the informal polite style ending -어 / 아요 (e.g. 좋아요, 좋았어요, 재미있어요, 재미있었어요, 먹어요, 먹었어요), including some set phrases with auxiliary verbs, such as -고 싶어요, -고 있어요, or -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 / 없어요, -(으)ㄹ 줄 알아요 / 몰라요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some honorific words and suffixes, such as 진지, 연세, 생신, 드세요, 선생님, 일어나세요 and humble words, for example, 저 / 제 as part of formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 안 가요, 못 해요), and replacing copula -예요 / 이에요 with its negative form -이 / 가 아니에요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and responding to teacher feedback on how to create textual cohesion, using elements such as conjunctions to sequence and link ideas and maintain the flow of expression, for example, 그리고, 그러나, 하지만, 그렇지만, 그래서, 그러므로

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the 2 numbering systems of Korean appropriately for purpose, for example, Korean native number, 하나, 둘, 셋, … and Sino-Korean number, 일, 이, 삼, …

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic counters and Arabic numerals with appropriate pronunciation (e.g. 사과 1 개 is read as 사과 한 개; 학생 3 명 is read as 학생 세 명; 11 살 is read as 열한 살; 7 학년 is read as 칠 학년), and comparing differences in word order between Korean and English when counting objects by conducting a role-play in a shopping situation, for example, 사과 한 개 compared with ‘one apple’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E12 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words to make questions, for example, 누가, 누구, 무엇, 언제, 어디, 어떻게, 왜, 몇, 무슨, 어느, 어떤

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E13 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between content words and function words, for example, in 나무가 예뻐요, 나무 and 예뻐요 are content words, and 가 is a function word

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E14 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions for greeting, farewelling and some learning activities and everyday interactions, for example, 안녕하세요? 만나서 반가워요 ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 고맙습니다 ; 감사합니다 ; 환영합니다 ; 어서 오세요 ; 생일 축하합니다 ; -계 ... 사람 as in 한국계 호주 사람, ... 회원이에요

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E04
as_extracts.description: They respond in Korean or English, and demonstrate their understanding of context, purpose and audience in texts.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Korean landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as 부산 (Pusan) which has the Sino-Korean meaning of 'Cauldron Mountain'

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, classifying and summarising information using text types (e.g. class surveys, notices, signs, images, timetables, graphics, charts, advertisements, brochures, leaflets, announcements), and presenting findings to others, for example, in a digital presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing a range of texts, such as promotional brochures, video clips, animations, comics, flyers and signs, websites and cards, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and practices, recognising features of language use in multimodal texts

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing information, collaboratively or independently, about people, times and activities, and using the information in new ways, for example, creating a timeline, diary, manual, instruction, procedure, timetable

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them in spoken or written Korean

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening, viewing, and reading for gist, context, and purpose, drawing on knowledge of types of text, context and language features to predict and confirm meaning, for example, the use of the imperative verb form -(으)세요, -해 보세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Korean that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a new aspect of a text for a story studied in class, such as a new character, place, plot, object, perspective or an alternative ending

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions about characters or settings in imaginative texts using structures such as ... 같아요, -은 / 는 것 같아요, for example, 뭐예요? ; 뭐 같아요? 호랑이 같아요. ; 좋은 것 같아요. ; 무서운 것 같아요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing patterns in language use associated with gender, age, social status or purpose, such as 형, 누나, 언니, 오빠, 나이 / 연세, 생일 / 생신, 선생님

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM05 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to Korean texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in ‘dictionary races’ to practise finding information in the dictionary quickly and accurately

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases, and noticing similarities and differences in language use (e.g. formality), for example, 안녕하세요? as opposed to 안녕? ; 안녕히 가세요 as opposed to 잘 가 ; 먹어 as opposed to 드세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools to identify words that do not have equivalents, such as ‘to wear’ in English and 입어요 (wear on the body), 써요 (wear on the head), 신어요 (wear on the feet), or ‘to open’ in English and 창문을 열어요 (open a window), 눈을 뜨세요 (please open your eyes), 책을 펴세요 (open the book)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing performances, such as music videos or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing cultural aspects and recording similarities and differences in interactions in similar contexts in their own culture(s)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how cultural concepts are expressed in non-literal word use, for example, 우리 (our) can be used to express inclusivity, for example, 우리집 (my/our house); 우리 학교 (my/our school); 우리나라 (my/our country)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing signage, posters and flashcards, displaying items such as the names of classroom objects, for example, 책, 공책, 의자, 책상, 가방, 연필, 지우개, 필통, 연필깎이

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of Hangeul and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing syllable blocks in different shapes, where a consonant and a vertical vowel are positioned side by side (e.g. 가), a horizontal vowel is positioned underneath a consonant (e.g. 누), or a consonant or a consonant cluster is added as a syllable-final consonant (e.g. 받침), under the first 2 types of syllable blocks, for example, 각, 눈, 닭

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining syllable blocks to write a word and applying spacing rules and basic phonological rules when reading and writing, for example, 친구가 교실에서 책을 읽어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple sentence structures in the ‘subject + object + verb’ order to make statements or ask questions, and inferring missing subjects or objects based on context, for example, 지금 무엇을 해요? is missing a subject, and 먹어요 is missing both a subject and an object

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to self and things appropriately using first-person pronouns 저, 제, 나, 내, 우리, demonstrative pronouns 이, 그, 저, 이것, 그것, 저것, or place pronouns 여기, 거기, 저기, for example, 이 사과가 맛있어요. ; 이것이 영어로 뭐예요? ; 여기가 우리 집이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic particles to mark case and other basic functions of nouns in a sentence, for example, -이 / 가, -을 / 를, -은 / 는, -에, -에서, -하고

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using present and past tenses with the informal polite style ending -어 / 아요 (e.g. 좋아요, 좋았어요, 재미있어요, 재미있었어요, 먹어요, 먹었어요), including some set phrases with auxiliary verbs, such as -고 싶어요, -고 있어요, or -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 / 없어요, -(으)ㄹ 줄 알아요 / 몰라요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some honorific words and suffixes, such as 진지, 연세, 생신, 드세요, 선생님, 일어나세요 and humble words, for example, 저 / 제 as part of formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 안 가요, 못 해요), and replacing copula -예요 / 이에요 with its negative form -이 / 가 아니에요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and responding to teacher feedback on how to create textual cohesion, using elements such as conjunctions to sequence and link ideas and maintain the flow of expression, for example, 그리고, 그러나, 하지만, 그렇지만, 그래서, 그러므로

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the 2 numbering systems of Korean appropriately for purpose, for example, Korean native number, 하나, 둘, 셋, … and Sino-Korean number, 일, 이, 삼, …

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic counters and Arabic numerals with appropriate pronunciation (e.g. 사과 1 개 is read as 사과 한 개; 학생 3 명 is read as 학생 세 명; 11 살 is read as 열한 살; 7 학년 is read as 칠 학년), and comparing differences in word order between Korean and English when counting objects by conducting a role-play in a shopping situation, for example, 사과 한 개 compared with ‘one apple’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E12 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words to make questions, for example, 누가, 누구, 무엇, 언제, 어디, 어떻게, 왜, 몇, 무슨, 어느, 어떤

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E13 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between content words and function words, for example, in 나무가 예뻐요, 나무 and 예뻐요 are content words, and 가 is a function word

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E14 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions for greeting, farewelling and some learning activities and everyday interactions, for example, 안녕하세요? 만나서 반가워요 ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 고맙습니다 ; 감사합니다 ; 환영합니다 ; 어서 오세요 ; 생일 축하합니다 ; -계 ... 사람 as in 한국계 호주 사람, ... 회원이에요

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E05
as_extracts.description: They use Hangeul with support, and familiar language, modelled sentences and grammatical structures to create texts appropriate to audience.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM01 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting and farewelling others, introducing themselves, expressing states of wellbeing, appreciation and wishes, using informal polite language appropriate for familiar people, for example, 안녕하세요? ; 저는 ... 예요 / 이에요. ; 만나서 반가워요. ; 12 살이에요. ; 7 학년이에요. ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing friends, family members or pets by presenting verbally about a personal topic chosen, for example, ... 있어요 / 없어요. ; 동생이 귀여워요. ; ... 은 / 는 예뻐요. ; ... 이 / 가 작아요. ; 눈이 커요. ; 머리가 갈색이에요. ; 다리가 짧아요. ; 귀가 길어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and comparing information about self and others, such as describing routines, likes/dislikes, events and leisure activities by conducting a class survey, for example, 6시에 일어나요. ; 주말에 (보통) 뭐 해요? ; 취미가 뭐예요? ; 뭐 좋아해요? ; 무슨 ... 을 / 를 좋아해요? ; 크리켓을 / 독서를 좋아해요. ; 수영을 / 영화를 안 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class about themselves, their family, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure activities; creating a graph representing the information they collected; and using the graph to communicate simple statements about the information gathered

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information through questioning and answering in a simple role-play with peers, for example, using 이것 / 저것이 뭐예요? ; ... 예요 / 이에요. ; ... 이 / 가 아니에요. ; 알아요, 몰라요, 네, 아니요, 맞아요, 틀려요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions using formulaic phrases (e.g. 제 생각에는 ...), for example, 제 생각에는 민수가 맞아요. ; 제 생각에는 그 영화가 재미있어요.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions and commands, for example, 일어나세요 ; 앉으세요 ; 쓰세요 ; 보세요 ; 잘 들으세요 ; 따라 하세요 ; 빨리 하세요 ; 조용히 하세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in classroom routines, such as responding to the teacher during roll call, for example, ... 있어요? 네, (여기) 있어요. / 아니요, 없어요. ; 왔어요? 아니요, -이 / 가 안 왔어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting by asking permission and making requests, for example, -을 / 를 빌려 주세요. ; -아도 / 어도 돼요? ; 괜찮아요? ; 미안해요. ; 고마워요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects such as making and playing a vocabulary game or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience, and making choices about when to use Korean or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for advice on how to express a word or concept in Korean or English, for example, … 이 / 가 / 은 / 는 영어 / 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising phone etiquette by performing a role-play of a phone conversation, for example, 여보세요, 저는 ... 입니다, 안녕히 계세요

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a video of people speaking Korean, identifying commonly used gestures and discussing their meaning and use

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flier for an upcoming event, such as 한글날, to promote Korean learning among school community members

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning events (e.g. a class celebration or a birthday party) with details such as day, time, place, activity and participants, for example, 월, 일, 요일, 시간, -에게, -로부터, 언제 / 어디에서 만나요? ; 누가 해요? ; 누구하고 해요? ; 같이 만들어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating real or simulated plans by conducting a personal conversation with peers using structures such as -고 싶어요 and -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요, for example, 무엇을 하고 싶어요? 영화를 보고 싶어요. ; 언제 갈 수 있어요? 주말에 갈 수 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in transactions, such as ordering or purchasing food, using -어 / 아요 or -(으)세요 form (e.g. 얼마예요? ; 아이스크림 한 개 주세요. ; 여기 있어요, 고맙습니다 / 감사합니다.) by participating in a role-play or an excursion to a Korean grocery shop

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions together, for example, participating in class or leisure activities such as sport/craft/dance/cooking; how to play 윷놀이 (e.g. 내 / 네 차례예요. ; 윷을 던지세요. ; 가세요. ; 도세요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a visual organisation board, including pictures, symbols or icons to represent different elements of a topic, and then explaining their choices to peers using spoken language or written descriptions, with the teacher using connecting words to sequence and link ideas

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM06 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions, using Hangeul with support

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling pictures of Korean and Australian classrooms and homes, highlighting differences in the arrangement of items, such as furniture and wall displays

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting orally or in writing on events in their immediate environments or personal worlds, such as a school or community event, celebration, excursion, or the arrival of a new student, for example, 우리 학교는 커요. ; 우리 반은 한국문화원에서 견학을 해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using multimodal presentation to report on Korean-speaking regions, such as creating a presentation about an area in Korea and incorporating graphs or tables representing important information about the region, for example, popular foods; leisure activities; industries and transport; for example, -이 / 가 유명해요 ; 날씨가 더워요 / 추워요 ; -가 / 이 많아요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a questionnaire that consists of a series of simple questions and response options, such as 있어요 / 없어요 ; 좋아해요 / 안 좋아해요 ; 할 수 있어요 / 없어요, and giving it to a Korean-speaking person visiting the school or in a secure online exchange to complete, as a way to gather information about family, home, interests and abilities, and presenting the responses in a podcast or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster in Korean to promote travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school, a guide to their favourite place, an explanation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names, or a history of their town; or reading a text and highlighting the text-type features they can see, before completing a jigsaw puzzle task with a similar text, placing all the elements of the text in the correct order using the text-type features as support

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing and classifying aspects of Australian culture for a Korean audience, for example, food and diet, daily life, significant places or cultural practices

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing and using bilingual texts for specific audiences (e.g. a big book or game for young learners of Korean; invitations to a class event; posters for a performance), noticing how meanings need to be tailored to take into account intended audience and cultural perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating stories in different modes, such as video clips or digital photo stories, based on real or imaginary characters, places and events

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and participating in dialogues (e.g. a script for a role-play or a play) and imagined interactions, and explaining the relationships between characters and contexts in a short drama or song, for example, 여우야, 여우야, 뭐 하니? / 여우님, 여우님, 뭐 해요?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of Hangeul and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing syllable blocks in different shapes, where a consonant and a vertical vowel are positioned side by side (e.g. 가), a horizontal vowel is positioned underneath a consonant (e.g. 누), or a consonant or a consonant cluster is added as a syllable-final consonant (e.g. 받침), under the first 2 types of syllable blocks, for example, 각, 눈, 닭

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining syllable blocks to write a word and applying spacing rules and basic phonological rules when reading and writing, for example, 친구가 교실에서 책을 읽어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple sentence structures in the ‘subject + object + verb’ order to make statements or ask questions, and inferring missing subjects or objects based on context, for example, 지금 무엇을 해요? is missing a subject, and 먹어요 is missing both a subject and an object

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to self and things appropriately using first-person pronouns 저, 제, 나, 내, 우리, demonstrative pronouns 이, 그, 저, 이것, 그것, 저것, or place pronouns 여기, 거기, 저기, for example, 이 사과가 맛있어요. ; 이것이 영어로 뭐예요? ; 여기가 우리 집이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic particles to mark case and other basic functions of nouns in a sentence, for example, -이 / 가, -을 / 를, -은 / 는, -에, -에서, -하고

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using present and past tenses with the informal polite style ending -어 / 아요 (e.g. 좋아요, 좋았어요, 재미있어요, 재미있었어요, 먹어요, 먹었어요), including some set phrases with auxiliary verbs, such as -고 싶어요, -고 있어요, or -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 / 없어요, -(으)ㄹ 줄 알아요 / 몰라요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some honorific words and suffixes, such as 진지, 연세, 생신, 드세요, 선생님, 일어나세요 and humble words, for example, 저 / 제 as part of formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 안 가요, 못 해요), and replacing copula -예요 / 이에요 with its negative form -이 / 가 아니에요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and responding to teacher feedback on how to create textual cohesion, using elements such as conjunctions to sequence and link ideas and maintain the flow of expression, for example, 그리고, 그러나, 하지만, 그렇지만, 그래서, 그러므로

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the 2 numbering systems of Korean appropriately for purpose, for example, Korean native number, 하나, 둘, 셋, … and Sino-Korean number, 일, 이, 삼, …

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic counters and Arabic numerals with appropriate pronunciation (e.g. 사과 1 개 is read as 사과 한 개; 학생 3 명 is read as 학생 세 명; 11 살 is read as 열한 살; 7 학년 is read as 칠 학년), and comparing differences in word order between Korean and English when counting objects by conducting a role-play in a shopping situation, for example, 사과 한 개 compared with ‘one apple’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E12 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words to make questions, for example, 누가, 누구, 무엇, 언제, 어디, 어떻게, 왜, 몇, 무슨, 어느, 어떤

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E13 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between content words and function words, for example, in 나무가 예뻐요, 나무 and 예뻐요 are content words, and 가 is a function word

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E14 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions for greeting, farewelling and some learning activities and everyday interactions, for example, 안녕하세요? 만나서 반가워요 ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 고맙습니다 ; 감사합니다 ; 환영합니다 ; 어서 오세요 ; 생일 축하합니다 ; -계 ... 사람 as in 한국계 호주 사람, ... 회원이에요

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E06
as_extracts.description: Students begin to use pronunciation, intonation and stress in spoken Korean to develop fluency.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL01 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken Korean to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and reproducing the sounds of Korean, noticing sound–symbol correspondence, for example, in consonants (발 as opposed to 팔; 갈 as opposed to 칼); in diphthongs transcribed as combinations of vowel letters (반가워요, 와요, 왜, 의사, 가위); in tense consonants transcribed by double-consonant letters (살 as opposed to 쌀, 자요 as opposed to 짜요, 고리 as opposed to 꼬리, 방 as opposed to 빵, 사요 as opposed to 싸요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences in intonation between statements, questions, requests and commands, for example, 가요. ; 가요? ; 가요!

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing understanding of the correct placement of letters in written form, as opposed to pronunciation in spoken form, through dictation practice, for example, 한국어가 재미있어요. [한구거가 재미읻써요] ; 옷이 예뻐요. [오시 예뻐요] ; 책을 읽어요. [채글 일거요]

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning Korean tongue twisters, for example, 네가 그린 기린 그림은 못 그린 기린 그림이고 내가 그린 기린 그림은 잘 그린 기린 그림이다. ; 경찰청 철창살은 외철창살이고 검찰청 철창살은 쌍철창살이다. ; 체다치즈를 최고 많이 먹은 최다은이 체다치즈 먹기 대회 최다 우승자이다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the pronunciation rules for syllable-final consonants, for example, that any consonant can be syllable-final, but there are only 7 syllable-final sounds [ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅇ]

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: knowing that for syllable-final double consonants, in most cases, only the first final consonant is pronounced, except for 닭 and 삶

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising using greetings appropriate to context and audience, for example, participating in a role-play activity, greeting members of the class using language appropriate to the role they have adopted (e.g. teacher, classmate, older neighbour, shop owner, cousin)

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E07
as_extracts.description: They demonstrate understanding of the conventions for Hangeul, non-verbal, spoken and written communication.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions and commands, for example, 일어나세요 ; 앉으세요 ; 쓰세요 ; 보세요 ; 잘 들으세요 ; 따라 하세요 ; 빨리 하세요 ; 조용히 하세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in classroom routines, such as responding to the teacher during roll call, for example, ... 있어요? 네, (여기) 있어요. / 아니요, 없어요. ; 왔어요? 아니요, -이 / 가 안 왔어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting by asking permission and making requests, for example, -을 / 를 빌려 주세요. ; -아도 / 어도 돼요? ; 괜찮아요? ; 미안해요. ; 고마워요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects such as making and playing a vocabulary game or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience, and making choices about when to use Korean or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for advice on how to express a word or concept in Korean or English, for example, … 이 / 가 / 은 / 는 영어 / 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising phone etiquette by performing a role-play of a phone conversation, for example, 여보세요, 저는 ... 입니다, 안녕히 계세요

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a video of people speaking Korean, identifying commonly used gestures and discussing their meaning and use

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flier for an upcoming event, such as 한글날, to promote Korean learning among school community members

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning events (e.g. a class celebration or a birthday party) with details such as day, time, place, activity and participants, for example, 월, 일, 요일, 시간, -에게, -로부터, 언제 / 어디에서 만나요? ; 누가 해요? ; 누구하고 해요? ; 같이 만들어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating real or simulated plans by conducting a personal conversation with peers using structures such as -고 싶어요 and -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요, for example, 무엇을 하고 싶어요? 영화를 보고 싶어요. ; 언제 갈 수 있어요? 주말에 갈 수 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in transactions, such as ordering or purchasing food, using -어 / 아요 or -(으)세요 form (e.g. 얼마예요? ; 아이스크림 한 개 주세요. ; 여기 있어요, 고맙습니다 / 감사합니다.) by participating in a role-play or an excursion to a Korean grocery shop

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions together, for example, participating in class or leisure activities such as sport/craft/dance/cooking; how to play 윷놀이 (e.g. 내 / 네 차례예요. ; 윷을 던지세요. ; 가세요. ; 도세요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a visual organisation board, including pictures, symbols or icons to represent different elements of a topic, and then explaining their choices to peers using spoken language or written descriptions, with the teacher using connecting words to sequence and link ideas

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Korean landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as 부산 (Pusan) which has the Sino-Korean meaning of 'Cauldron Mountain'

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, classifying and summarising information using text types (e.g. class surveys, notices, signs, images, timetables, graphics, charts, advertisements, brochures, leaflets, announcements), and presenting findings to others, for example, in a digital presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing a range of texts, such as promotional brochures, video clips, animations, comics, flyers and signs, websites and cards, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and practices, recognising features of language use in multimodal texts

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sequencing information, collaboratively or independently, about people, times and activities, and using the information in new ways, for example, creating a timeline, diary, manual, instruction, procedure, timetable

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to, reading or viewing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander authors’ stories in English and responding to them in spoken or written Korean

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP3
organising_ideas.text: The significant and ongoing contributions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and their histories and cultures are acknowledged locally, nationally and globally.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening, viewing, and reading for gist, context, and purpose, drawing on knowledge of types of text, context and language features to predict and confirm meaning, for example, the use of the imperative verb form -(으)세요, -해 보세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the ways words can be misinterpreted, for example, the naming of the Barwon River in English (Wadawurrung word Parwan for ‘magpie’), or the Yarra River (Wurundjeri term Yarro Yarro, meaning ‘it flows’), and identifying ‘false friends’ or commonly misunderstood terms and phrases in Korean that can cause miscommunication

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: inventing a new aspect of a text for a story studied in class, such as a new character, place, plot, object, perspective or an alternative ending

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions about characters or settings in imaginative texts using structures such as ... 같아요, -은 / 는 것 같아요, for example, 뭐예요? ; 뭐 같아요? 호랑이 같아요. ; 좋은 것 같아요. ; 무서운 것 같아요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and discussing patterns in language use associated with gender, age, social status or purpose, such as 형, 누나, 언니, 오빠, 나이 / 연세, 생일 / 생신, 선생님

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM05 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: develop and apply strategies to interpret and respond to Korean texts, and to convey meaning and intercultural understanding in Korean in familiar contexts
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in ‘dictionary races’ to practise finding information in the dictionary quickly and accurately

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases, and noticing similarities and differences in language use (e.g. formality), for example, 안녕하세요? as opposed to 안녕? ; 안녕히 가세요 as opposed to 잘 가 ; 먹어 as opposed to 드세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools to identify words that do not have equivalents, such as ‘to wear’ in English and 입어요 (wear on the body), 써요 (wear on the head), 신어요 (wear on the feet), or ‘to open’ in English and 창문을 열어요 (open a window), 눈을 뜨세요 (please open your eyes), 책을 펴세요 (open the book)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing performances, such as music videos or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing cultural aspects and recording similarities and differences in interactions in similar contexts in their own culture(s)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how cultural concepts are expressed in non-literal word use, for example, 우리 (our) can be used to express inclusivity, for example, 우리집 (my/our house); 우리 학교 (my/our school); 우리나라 (my/our country)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing signage, posters and flashcards, displaying items such as the names of classroom objects, for example, 책, 공책, 의자, 책상, 가방, 연필, 지우개, 필통, 연필깎이

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM06 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions, using Hangeul with support

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling pictures of Korean and Australian classrooms and homes, highlighting differences in the arrangement of items, such as furniture and wall displays

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting orally or in writing on events in their immediate environments or personal worlds, such as a school or community event, celebration, excursion, or the arrival of a new student, for example, 우리 학교는 커요. ; 우리 반은 한국문화원에서 견학을 해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using multimodal presentation to report on Korean-speaking regions, such as creating a presentation about an area in Korea and incorporating graphs or tables representing important information about the region, for example, popular foods; leisure activities; industries and transport; for example, -이 / 가 유명해요 ; 날씨가 더워요 / 추워요 ; -가 / 이 많아요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a questionnaire that consists of a series of simple questions and response options, such as 있어요 / 없어요 ; 좋아해요 / 안 좋아해요 ; 할 수 있어요 / 없어요, and giving it to a Korean-speaking person visiting the school or in a secure online exchange to complete, as a way to gather information about family, home, interests and abilities, and presenting the responses in a podcast or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster in Korean to promote travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: producing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school, a guide to their favourite place, an explanation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names, or a history of their town; or reading a text and highlighting the text-type features they can see, before completing a jigsaw puzzle task with a similar text, placing all the elements of the text in the correct order using the text-type features as support

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing and classifying aspects of Australian culture for a Korean audience, for example, food and diet, daily life, significant places or cultural practices

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing and using bilingual texts for specific audiences (e.g. a big book or game for young learners of Korean; invitations to a class event; posters for a performance), noticing how meanings need to be tailored to take into account intended audience and cultural perspectives

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating stories in different modes, such as video clips or digital photo stories, based on real or imaginary characters, places and events

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: composing and participating in dialogues (e.g. a script for a role-play or a play) and imagined interactions, and explaining the relationships between characters and contexts in a short drama or song, for example, 여우야, 여우야, 뭐 하니? / 여우님, 여우님, 뭐 해요?

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL01 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise and apply the sounds and conventions of spoken Korean to develop fluency, and to respond to and create simple texts in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and reproducing the sounds of Korean, noticing sound–symbol correspondence, for example, in consonants (발 as opposed to 팔; 갈 as opposed to 칼); in diphthongs transcribed as combinations of vowel letters (반가워요, 와요, 왜, 의사, 가위); in tense consonants transcribed by double-consonant letters (살 as opposed to 쌀, 자요 as opposed to 짜요, 고리 as opposed to 꼬리, 방 as opposed to 빵, 사요 as opposed to 싸요)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the differences in intonation between statements, questions, requests and commands, for example, 가요. ; 가요? ; 가요!

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: showing understanding of the correct placement of letters in written form, as opposed to pronunciation in spoken form, through dictation practice, for example, 한국어가 재미있어요. [한구거가 재미읻써요] ; 옷이 예뻐요. [오시 예뻐요] ; 책을 읽어요. [채글 일거요]

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: learning Korean tongue twisters, for example, 네가 그린 기린 그림은 못 그린 기린 그림이고 내가 그린 기린 그림은 잘 그린 기린 그림이다. ; 경찰청 철창살은 외철창살이고 검찰청 철창살은 쌍철창살이다. ; 체다치즈를 최고 많이 먹은 최다은이 체다치즈 먹기 대회 최다 우승자이다.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using the pronunciation rules for syllable-final consonants, for example, that any consonant can be syllable-final, but there are only 7 syllable-final sounds [ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ, ㅁ, ㅂ, ㅇ]

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: knowing that for syllable-final double consonants, in most cases, only the first final consonant is pronounced, except for 닭 and 삶

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL01-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising using greetings appropriate to context and audience, for example, participating in a role-play activity, greeting members of the class using language appropriate to the role they have adopted (e.g. teacher, classmate, older neighbour, shop owner, cousin)

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL02 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: apply understanding of Hangeul and grammatical structures to respond to and create a range of texts using conventions appropriate to audience and text type

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing syllable blocks in different shapes, where a consonant and a vertical vowel are positioned side by side (e.g. 가), a horizontal vowel is positioned underneath a consonant (e.g. 누), or a consonant or a consonant cluster is added as a syllable-final consonant (e.g. 받침), under the first 2 types of syllable blocks, for example, 각, 눈, 닭

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: combining syllable blocks to write a word and applying spacing rules and basic phonological rules when reading and writing, for example, 친구가 교실에서 책을 읽어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and using simple sentence structures in the ‘subject + object + verb’ order to make statements or ask questions, and inferring missing subjects or objects based on context, for example, 지금 무엇을 해요? is missing a subject, and 먹어요 is missing both a subject and an object

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: referring to self and things appropriately using first-person pronouns 저, 제, 나, 내, 우리, demonstrative pronouns 이, 그, 저, 이것, 그것, 저것, or place pronouns 여기, 거기, 저기, for example, 이 사과가 맛있어요. ; 이것이 영어로 뭐예요? ; 여기가 우리 집이에요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic particles to mark case and other basic functions of nouns in a sentence, for example, -이 / 가, -을 / 를, -은 / 는, -에, -에서, -하고

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using present and past tenses with the informal polite style ending -어 / 아요 (e.g. 좋아요, 좋았어요, 재미있어요, 재미있었어요, 먹어요, 먹었어요), including some set phrases with auxiliary verbs, such as -고 싶어요, -고 있어요, or -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 / 없어요, -(으)ㄹ 줄 알아요 / 몰라요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using some honorific words and suffixes, such as 진지, 연세, 생신, 드세요, 선생님, 일어나세요 and humble words, for example, 저 / 제 as part of formulaic expressions

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using simple negation by placing 안 or 못 before a verb (e.g. 안 가요, 못 해요), and replacing copula -예요 / 이에요 with its negative form -이 / 가 아니에요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and responding to teacher feedback on how to create textual cohesion, using elements such as conjunctions to sequence and link ideas and maintain the flow of expression, for example, 그리고, 그러나, 하지만, 그렇지만, 그래서, 그러므로

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the 2 numbering systems of Korean appropriately for purpose, for example, Korean native number, 하나, 둘, 셋, … and Sino-Korean number, 일, 이, 삼, …

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E11 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using basic counters and Arabic numerals with appropriate pronunciation (e.g. 사과 1 개 is read as 사과 한 개; 학생 3 명 is read as 학생 세 명; 11 살 is read as 열한 살; 7 학년 is read as 칠 학년), and comparing differences in word order between Korean and English when counting objects by conducting a role-play in a shopping situation, for example, 사과 한 개 compared with ‘one apple’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E12 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using question words to make questions, for example, 누가, 누구, 무엇, 언제, 어디, 어떻게, 왜, 몇, 무슨, 어느, 어떤

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E13 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discriminating between content words and function words, for example, in 나무가 예뻐요, 나무 and 예뻐요 are content words, and 가 is a function word

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL02-E14 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using idiomatic expressions for greeting, farewelling and some learning activities and everyday interactions, for example, 안녕하세요? 만나서 반가워요 ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요 ; 고맙습니다 ; 감사합니다 ; 환영합니다 ; 어서 오세요 ; 생일 축하합니다 ; -계 ... 사람 as in 한국계 호주 사람, ... 회원이에요

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL04 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: recognise how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values
content_descriptions.sub_strand: Understanding the interrelationship of language and culture

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in a guided discussion of the roles of and relationships between culture and language with reference to Korean, English and other known languages, and discussing, questioning and explaining understanding of other cultures, including Korean culture, without stereotyping

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a ‘language portrait’ of themselves through the use of a whole-body silhouette, where students represent their personal experiences of language and culture by adding colours, shapes and words within and around the outline

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place on which they live and incorporating this into their self-introduction in Korean

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: viewing interactions in Korean between peers or in multimodal texts such as a film segment, noticing and recording cultural similarities and differences between interactions in Korean and in their own culture(s), for example, comparing similarities and differences between cultures using a Venn diagram

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying words that have similar meanings and pronunciation across different languages, reflecting on the possible origins and cultural associations of such words, for example, 엄마, ‘mum’, ‘mama’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on, in Korean or English, how Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages have strong connections to Country or Place and how these can be compared with language variations across Korean-speaking communities

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying non-verbal expressions taken for granted in communication in different cultures, for example, making or avoiding eye contact depending on the social context; bowing to an older person; nodding to show agreement; pointing and beckoning with appropriate hand gestures

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E08 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: becoming aware of the variety of gender-inclusive ways in which people can be addressed, including the use of non-gendered expressions such as 그 사람, 그, or 그 분 (honorific) which can apply to all Korean speakers, and if the name is known, referring to them by their name with the suffix 씨 where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E09 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reflecting on the cultural associations of individual Korean words which may be interpreted differently by people who do not know Korean culture, for example, 우리 (our) can be used for 우리 선생님 (my teacher) and 우리나라 (my country), and kinship terms such as 형, 오빠, 누나, 언니 and 이모 are often used to address other people

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL04-E10 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring how politeness is expressed differently in Korean and English language, such as the importance of age, social status and levels of formality, and understanding the significance of social conventions and cultural concepts, for example, using 식사하셨어요? as a greeting

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E08
as_extracts.description: They comment on aspects of Korean and English language structures and features, using some metalanguage.

content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8UL03 - Korean
content_descriptions.text: compare the structures and features of Korean with English and/or other languages using some metalanguage

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the purpose, intended audience and key language features of short texts such as road signs or instructions, and comparing these with English versions of similar texts, for example, 천천히 as opposed to ‘drive slowly’; 미세요 / 당기세요 as opposed to ‘push’/‘pull’

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using metalanguage to identify conventions of familiar text types, such as letters, emails or greeting/invitation cards, and comparing them with English, for example, salutations, the order of elements in an address, and format of the date and time, for example, ... 에게, ... 로부터, 4 월 3 일 금요일, 오후 다섯 시

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the similarities in key features of Korean and English texts such as stories, songs and conversation, for example, 옛날 옛날에, 오래오래 행복하게 살았대요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing how differently abbreviated forms in multimedia and teacher-curated social media are accepted in Korean and English and/or other languages, for example, 쌤, 여친, 남친, 셀카

elaborations.name: VC2LK8UL03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting and analysing samples of language from multimodal texts to explore differences in communicative style and expression between social groups in Korean and Australian cultures, for example, 어서 오세요 to mean ‘Welcome’, and 밥 먹었어요? to mean ‘How are you?’

as_extracts.name: LKOR7108-E09
as_extracts.description: They understand how aspects of language and culture contribute to their own and others’ identity.

content_descriptions.text: recognise how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), beliefs, attitudes and values

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM01 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: interact with others using modelled language to exchange information in familiar contexts about themselves and their personal worlds

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: greeting and farewelling others, introducing themselves, expressing states of wellbeing, appreciation and wishes, using informal polite language appropriate for familiar people, for example, 안녕하세요? ; 저는 ... 예요 / 이에요. ; 만나서 반가워요. ; 12 살이에요. ; 7 학년이에요. ; 안녕히 가세요 / 계세요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: describing friends, family members or pets by presenting verbally about a personal topic chosen, for example, ... 있어요 / 없어요. ; 동생이 귀여워요. ; ... 은 / 는 예뻐요. ; ... 이 / 가 작아요. ; 눈이 커요. ; 머리가 갈색이에요. ; 다리가 짧아요. ; 귀가 길어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing and comparing information about self and others, such as describing routines, likes/dislikes, events and leisure activities by conducting a class survey, for example, 6시에 일어나요. ; 주말에 (보통) 뭐 해요? ; 취미가 뭐예요? ; 뭐 좋아해요? ; 무슨 ... 을 / 를 좋아해요? ; 크리켓을 / 독서를 좋아해요. ; 수영을 / 영화를 안 좋아해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interviewing members of the class about themselves, their family, pets, likes and dislikes, hobbies and leisure activities; creating a graph representing the information they collected; and using the graph to communicate simple statements about the information gathered

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: exchanging information through questioning and answering in a simple role-play with peers, for example, using 이것 / 저것이 뭐예요? ; ... 예요 / 이에요. ; ... 이 / 가 아니에요. ; 알아요, 몰라요, 네, 아니요, 맞아요, 틀려요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM01-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing opinions using formulaic phrases (e.g. 제 생각에는 ...), for example, 제 생각에는 민수가 맞아요. ; 제 생각에는 그 영화가 재미있어요.

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM02 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines and tasks related to their classroom and interests

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following instructions and commands, for example, 일어나세요 ; 앉으세요 ; 쓰세요 ; 보세요 ; 잘 들으세요 ; 따라 하세요 ; 빨리 하세요 ; 조용히 하세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting in classroom routines, such as responding to the teacher during roll call, for example, ... 있어요? 네, (여기) 있어요. / 아니요, 없어요. ; 왔어요? 아니요, -이 / 가 안 왔어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: interacting by asking permission and making requests, for example, -을 / 를 빌려 주세요. ; -아도 / 어도 돼요? ; 괜찮아요? ; 미안해요. ; 고마워요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in collaborative projects such as making and playing a vocabulary game or producing and sharing a digital alphabet or number book for a younger audience, and making choices about when to use Korean or English depending on the context, topic and nature of the interaction

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: asking for advice on how to express a word or concept in Korean or English, for example, … 이 / 가 / 은 / 는 영어 / 한국어로 뭐예요?

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM02-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: practising phone etiquette by performing a role-play of a phone conversation, for example, 여보세요, 저는 ... 입니다, 안녕히 계세요

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM03 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: engage in modelled spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: watching a video of people speaking Korean, identifying commonly used gestures and discussing their meaning and use

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: working with peers to produce a bilingual publicity flier for an upcoming event, such as 한글날, to promote Korean learning among school community members

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning events (e.g. a class celebration or a birthday party) with details such as day, time, place, activity and participants, for example, 월, 일, 요일, 시간, -에게, -로부터, 언제 / 어디에서 만나요? ; 누가 해요? ; 누구하고 해요? ; 같이 만들어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: negotiating real or simulated plans by conducting a personal conversation with peers using structures such as -고 싶어요 and -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요, for example, 무엇을 하고 싶어요? 영화를 보고 싶어요. ; 언제 갈 수 있어요? 주말에 갈 수 있어요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in transactions, such as ordering or purchasing food, using -어 / 아요 or -(으)세요 form (e.g. 얼마예요? ; 아이스크림 한 개 주세요. ; 여기 있어요, 고맙습니다 / 감사합니다.) by participating in a role-play or an excursion to a Korean grocery shop

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: following procedures and instructions together, for example, participating in class or leisure activities such as sport/craft/dance/cooking; how to play 윷놀이 (e.g. 내 / 네 차례예요. ; 윷을 던지세요. ; 가세요. ; 도세요.)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM03-E07 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a visual organisation board, including pictures, symbols or icons to represent different elements of a topic, and then explaining their choices to peers using spoken language or written descriptions, with the teacher using connecting words to sequence and link ideas

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM04 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: locate information and ideas in familiar spoken, written, viewed and multimodal texts, responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience
substrand_content_descriptions.sub_strand: Mediating meaning in and between languages

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: noticing how local names of streets, places and landmarks can have their origins in language(s) of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying the meanings of these place names, for example, ‘You Yangs’ comes from the Wadawurrung words Wurdi Youang, meaning ‘big hill’, and then discussing the names of Korean landforms that also denote physical characteristics, such as 부산 (Pusan) which has the Sino-Korean meaning of 'Cauldron Mountain'

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: locating, classifying and summarising information using text types (e.g. class surveys, notices, signs, images, timetables, graphics, charts, advertisements, brochures, leaflets, announcements), and presenting findings to others, for example, in a digital presentation, poster or wall chart

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and viewing a range of texts, such as promotional brochures, video clips, animations, comics, flyers and signs, websites and cards, to obtain and compile information about places, lifestyles and practices, recognising features of language use in multimodal texts

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM04-E04 - Korean

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: participating in ‘dictionary races’ to practise finding information in the dictionary quickly and accurately

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: translating short personal texts, identifying words and phrases, and noticing similarities and differences in language use (e.g. formality), for example, 안녕하세요? as opposed to 안녕? ; 안녕히 가세요 as opposed to 잘 가 ; 먹어 as opposed to 드세요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using bilingual dictionaries and online translation tools to identify words that do not have equivalents, such as ‘to wear’ in English and 입어요 (wear on the body), 써요 (wear on the head), 신어요 (wear on the feet), or ‘to open’ in English and 창문을 열어요 (open a window), 눈을 뜨세요 (please open your eyes), 책을 펴세요 (open the book)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: listening to and viewing performances, such as music videos or extracts from films, sharing reactions with peers, noticing cultural aspects and recording similarities and differences in interactions in similar contexts in their own culture(s)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing how cultural concepts are expressed in non-literal word use, for example, 우리 (our) can be used to express inclusivity, for example, 우리집 (my/our house); 우리 학교 (my/our school); 우리나라 (my/our country)

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM05-E06 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing signage, posters and flashcards, displaying items such as the names of classroom objects, for example, 책, 공책, 의자, 책상, 가방, 연필, 지우개, 필통, 연필깎이

substrand_content_descriptions.name: VC2LK8CM06 - Korean
substrand_content_descriptions.text: create spoken and written texts using appropriate vocabulary, expressions and grammatical structures, and some textual conventions, using Hangeul with support

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E01 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: labelling pictures of Korean and Australian classrooms and homes, highlighting differences in the arrangement of items, such as furniture and wall displays

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E02 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: reporting orally or in writing on events in their immediate environments or personal worlds, such as a school or community event, celebration, excursion, or the arrival of a new student, for example, 우리 학교는 커요. ; 우리 반은 한국문화원에서 견학을 해요.

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E03 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: using multimodal presentation to report on Korean-speaking regions, such as creating a presentation about an area in Korea and incorporating graphs or tables representing important information about the region, for example, popular foods; leisure activities; industries and transport; for example, -이 / 가 유명해요 ; 날씨가 더워요 / 추워요 ; -가 / 이 많아요

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E04 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: compiling a questionnaire that consists of a series of simple questions and response options, such as 있어요 / 없어요 ; 좋아해요 / 안 좋아해요 ; 할 수 있어요 / 없어요, and giving it to a Korean-speaking person visiting the school or in a secure online exchange to complete, as a way to gather information about family, home, interests and abilities, and presenting the responses in a podcast or newsletter

elaborations.name: VC2LK8CM06-E05 - Korean
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a poster in Korean to promote travel to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander Country or Place, including what to see and do

elaborations.elaboration_text: producing an informative text introducing an aspect of their immediate environment or personal worlds, for example, creating a tour of their school, a guide to their favourite place, an explanation of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander place names, or a history of their town; or reading a text and highlighting the text-type features they can see, before completing a jigsaw puzzle task with a similar text, placing all the elements of the text in the correct order using the text-type features as support
